abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: A four-user quantum spine-leaf network over up to 540-km fiber is demonstrated using twin-field QKD, achieving full connectivity and high secret key rates.
motivation: Long-distance quantum communication networks are essential for practical quantum internet, but scaling to multiple users over hundreds of kilometers remains challenging.
method: The authors implement a spine-leaf network architecture with twin-field QKD protocol operating at 1.25 GHz clock rate, using photonic integrated circuits for stability and scalability.
result: The network supports full connections between any two user pairs over up to 540 km fiber, with a secret key rate of 9.38 × 10⁻⁹ bit per pulse.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a scalable and practical quantum network architecture that can be deployed over existing fiber infrastructure, advancing toward a global quantum internet.

title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a transmon qubit, and an NV center ensemble, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe characteristic three-mode avoided crossings, indicating strong coupling between all three components, and extract coupling strengths and cooperativities.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable platform for hybrid quantum networks and quantum transducers, enabling coherent interactions between superconducting and spin systems.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
authors: Vasco Cavina And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: A non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model with squeezed and displaced reservoirs is introduced, enabling work extraction, stochastic time-dependence, and a fluctuation theorem for heat statistics.
motivation: To extend the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium reservoirs, capturing work and heat effects beyond standard equilibrium assumptions.
method: The model uses squeezed and displaced thermal modes; a modified Keldysh contour treats squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians to compute full heat statistics.
result: Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs generate effective time-dependence and pure work; squeezing breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, reconciled with the second law by accounting for initial non-equilibrium energy. A fluctuation theorem for energy balance is proven.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile framework for quantum thermodynamics with non-equilibrium reservoirs, showing quantum-classical correspondence and thermodynamic symmetries.

title: Work Statistics Under Quantum-Jump And Quench Dynamics In Monitored Ising Chains
authors: Alessandro Silva Manali Malakar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate work statistics in monitored transverse-field Ising chains subject to both a quantum quench of the transverse field and either stochastic quantum jumps or controlled measurement sequences. For generalized measurements, we derive a trajectory-resolved generating function for work statistics in the two-point energy measurement scheme. Evaluating it using a fermionic Gaussian-state formalism, we show that, under stochastic jump dynamics, the work distribution crosses over from a comb-like structure to an essentially Gaussian form with shrinking sub-Gaussian tails, as the number of detection events grows. For controlled jump protocols, the energy added by each jump is constant when successive jumps are causally disconnected but decreases and then saturates when they lie within each other's light cone, yielding linear and sublinear growth of the average work, respectively. For monitored quenches, continuous observation washes out the fine structure of the isolated-quench distribution and again drives the statistics toward Gaussian behavior.
tldr: This paper studies work statistics in monitored transverse-field Ising chains under quantum jumps and quenches, revealing crossovers from comb-like to Gaussian distributions and sublinear work growth due to causal light-cone effects.
motivation: Understanding work statistics in monitored quantum systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics, especially in the context of measurement-induced dynamics and feedback control.
method: The authors derive a trajectory-resolved generating function for work statistics using a fermionic Gaussian-state formalism and analyze both stochastic quantum jumps and controlled measurement sequences.
result: Under stochastic jumps, the work distribution transitions from comb-like to Gaussian with shrinking tails; under controlled jumps, average work grows linearly when jumps are causally disconnected and sublinearly when they lie within each other's light cone.
conclusion: Continuous monitoring washes out fine structure and drives work statistics toward Gaussian behavior, providing insights into the interplay of measurement and thermodynamics in quantum systems.

title: Classification And Exact Local Masking In Finite-Field Clifford Dual-Unitary Circuits
authors: Basanta R Pahari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify two-qudit finite-field Clifford dual-unitary gates and apply the classification to exact local masking and operator transport in homogeneous brickwork circuits. Under ordered one-qudit Clifford equivalence, the dual-unitary locus contains [MATH] perfect-tensor cores, one rank-one core, and one SWAP core. The perfect cores are indexed by \[ \delta=\det B=\det C, \] and are related to the ordered cross-ratio [MATH] of the associated [MATH] MDS configuration through \[ \lambda={\delta-1}. \] Homogeneous repetition separates these cores into five transport phases whose algebraic codimensions in [MATH] are [MATH]. The one-site Weyl edge channels determine exact local-masking distances. Perfect-tensor circuits attain \[ d_1(t)=4t, \qquad d_2(t)=4t-2, \] whereas delayed erasers satisfy \[ d_1(t)=4t-2, \qquad d_2(t)=4t-4 \] for [MATH]. Consequently, sufficiently short quantum messages are completely hidden from every one- or two-qudit output subsystem, even when the input is entangled with a reference, while remaining exactly recoverable from the full output. For [MATH], we construct an explicit perfect-tensor Clifford gate from two inverse SUM gates. Exhaustive Weyl-support searches for [MATH] reproduce the predicted masking distances, and a one-period Choi-channel calculation for a four-qutrit periodic circuit gives numerical residual leakage below [MATH]. Under the coherent perturbation considered here, local leakage is linear in the perturbation strength, whereas the infidelity of recovery using the ideal inverse is quadratic near the perfect point.
tldr: Classifies two-qudit Clifford dual-unitary gates over finite fields and applies them to exact local masking and operator transport in brickwork circuits.
motivation: Understanding the structure of dual-unitary gates and their ability to hide quantum information locally is important for quantum information processing and cryptography.
method: Uses algebraic classification of Clifford dual-unitary gates via ordered one-qudit Clifford equivalence, and analyzes operator transport and local masking distances in homogeneous brickwork circuits.
result: Identifies perfect-tensor cores and their transport phases; shows that perfect-tensor circuits achieve exact local masking distances d1(t)=4t and d2(t)=4t-2, while delayed erasers achieve d1(t)=4t-2 and d2(t)=4t-4.
conclusion: Short quantum messages can be completely hidden from every one- or two-qudit output subsystem while remaining recoverable from the full output, with implications for quantum secret sharing and information hiding.

The perfect cores are indexed by δ = det B = det C and related to the ordered cross-ratio λ = δ/(δ-1) of the associated [4,2,3]_q MDS configuration. Homogeneous repetition separates these cores into five transport phases with algebraic codimensions 0,1,2,3,4 in Sp(4,q). The one-site Weyl edge channels determine exact local-masking distances: perfect-tensor circuits achieve d1(t)=4t and d2(t)=4t-2, while delayed erasers satisfy d1(t)=4t-2 and d2(t)=4t-4 for t≥2. Consequently, sufficiently short quantum messages are completely hidden from every one- or two-qudit output subsystem, even when the input is entangled with a reference, while remaining exactly recoverable from the full output. For q=3, an explicit perfect-tensor Clifford gate is constructed from two inverse SUM gates. title: Robust Quantum Memory Advantage From Contextuality
authors: Shiroman Prakash
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum contextuality is widely recognized as an essential non-classical resource underlying quantum technology, yet illuminating the precise mechanisms through which it translates into unconditional computational advantages remains an ongoing challenge. We demonstrate an exponential, noise-resilient memory advantage for quantum finite automata arising from graph-theoretic approaches to contextuality. We define a promise problem on an exclusivity graph [MATH] for which any classical deterministic automaton acts as a non-contextual hidden variable model requiring at least [MATH] states, where [MATH] is the graph's chromatic number. In contrast, by exploiting a structural phenomenon we term , a QFA solves this task using a memory of dimension at most [MATH], where [MATH] is the graph's orthogonal rank. This separation scales exponentially ([MATH] versus [MATH]) for Boolean-orthogonality graphs. Crucially, this memory advantage maintains an [MATH] threshold against both depolarizing and coherent noise.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an exponential, noise-resilient memory advantage for quantum finite automata using graph-theoretic contextuality.
motivation: To understand how quantum contextuality translates into unconditional computational advantages, particularly in memory-limited settings.
method: Defines a promise problem on an exclusivity graph and shows that classical automata require at least the chromatic number of states, while quantum automata require only the orthogonal rank, exploiting a structural phenomenon called 'robust quantum memory advantage'.
result: The separation scales exponentially for Boolean-orthogonality graphs, and the advantage persists under depolarizing and coherent noise up to a threshold.
conclusion: Contextuality provides a robust quantum memory advantage, highlighting its role as a resource for quantum computation.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper establishes an exponential, noise-resilient memory advantage for quantum finite automata (QFA) over classical deterministic automata, rooted in quantum contextuality. The authors define a promise problem on an exclusivity graph G, where classical automata require at least N = χ(G) states (the chromatic number), while a QFA solves it using d = ξ(G) + 1 states (the orthogonal rank plus one). For Boolean-orthogonality graphs, this yields an exponential separation: d = O(n) versus N = 2^{Ω(n)}. The advantage persists under depolarizing and coherent noise with an O(1) threshold, demonstrating robustness. The key concept is 'representational contextuality,' a structural phenomenon that enables the QFA to exploit contextuality without requiring measurement or state update, thus achieving a memory advantage in a one-way automaton model.
key_contributions: Defines a promise problem on exclusivity graphs that separates classical and quantum finite automata memory requirements.
Introduces the concept of 'representational contextuality' as a mechanism for quantum advantage in automata.
Proves an exponential separation (d = O(n) vs N = 2^{Ω(n)}) for Boolean-orthogonality graphs.
Demonstrates noise resilience with an O(1) threshold against depolarizing and coherent noise.
Connects graph-theoretic contextuality (via exclusivity graphs) to computational advantages in finite automata.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper uses graph-theoretic tools to model contextuality, specifically exclusivity graphs where vertices represent events and edges denote exclusivity. The promise problem is defined such that classical automata correspond to non-contextual hidden variable models, requiring a number of states equal to the chromatic number χ(G). The QFA exploits the orthogonal rank ξ(G) of the graph, encoding quantum states that satisfy exclusivity constraints via orthogonal vectors. The automaton model is a one-way QFA with a fixed unitary evolution and projective measurement at the end, but no intermediate measurements, making it a 'measure-once' model. The analysis of noise resilience uses depolarizing and coherent noise channels, showing that the advantage persists as long as noise strength is below a constant threshold.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is an exponential separation in memory size: for a family of Boolean-orthogonality graphs (e.g., the orthogonality graph of n-dimensional hypercube), χ(G) = 2^{Ω(n)} while ξ(G) = O(n), so classical automata need exponentially more states. The QFA uses d = ξ(G) + 1 = O(n) states. Under noise, the success probability remains above 2/3 for depolarizing noise with strength p < 1/2 and coherent noise with strength θ < π/4, providing an O(1) threshold. The paper also shows that the advantage is robust to small perturbations, as the QFA's success probability decays linearly with noise strength.
strengths: Provides a clean, graph-theoretic characterization of contextuality-based quantum advantage.
Achieves exponential separation with a simple automaton model, highlighting fundamental differences in memory.
Includes noise analysis showing constant threshold, demonstrating practical relevance.
Introduces 'representational contextuality' as a new concept that may have broader implications.
limitations: The promise problem is somewhat artificial and may not correspond to natural computational tasks.
The QFA model is restricted (measure-once), and the advantage may not extend to more general quantum models.
The noise analysis assumes specific noise models; more general noise or adversarial noise is not considered.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses quantum contextuality, a core topic in quantum foundations, and demonstrates its operational power in a computational setting (quantum finite automata). It connects to quantum information theory by quantifying memory advantages and noise resilience, and to quantum physics by using exclusivity graphs, a tool from contextuality studies. The results align with the researcher's interest in quantum phenomena and their technological implications.

The concept of representational contextuality is novel and may inspire further work. The paper is well-structured, clear, and technically sound. It is likely to influence both quantum foundations and quantum computing theory.

title: Surface Charges In A Rydberg Atom-nanowaveguide Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Aswathy Raj, Anna Kortel, Krishna Jadeja, Dylan J. Brown, Alexey Vylegzhanin, Robert L\"ow, S\'ile Nic Chormaic
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid quantum platforms based on highly excited Rydberg atoms coupled to nanophotonics devices offer a promising route toward scalable quantum networks and integrated quantum technologies. However, the close proximity of Rydberg atoms to dielectric nanostructures makes these systems particularly susceptible to uncontrolled surface electric fields that can lead to a degradation of the excitation process. Here, we experimentally investigate Rydberg excitation of laser-cooled [MATH]Rb atoms via the evanescent field of an optical nanofiber in the presence of fiber-guided red- and blue-detuned light fields as used to trap ground state atoms in fiber-based dipole traps. We observe a time evolution of the Rydberg excitation spectrum when both the dipole trapping fields are on and the additional spectral features that appear can be suppressed by applying an external oscillating electric field to the system, strongly indicating that surface charge accumulation is responsible for the observed spectral feature. The experimental results are reproduced qualitatively by a model that incorporates DC energy level shifts arising from electric fields generated by charges deposited on the nanofiber surface. We identify Rydberg-ground state collisional ionization, which is enhanced by the dipole trapping fields, as the dominant mechanism for charge generation. These results provide new insight into charge dynamics at dielectric nanophotonic interfaces and establish practical guidelines for mitigating surface charge-induced electric fields in fiber-integrated Rydberg quantum systems.
tldr: This paper experimentally investigates surface charge effects in a Rydberg atom-nanofiber hybrid system and demonstrates mitigation via oscillating electric fields.
motivation: Hybrid quantum platforms combining Rydberg atoms with nanophotonics are promising for quantum networks, but surface charges on dielectric nanostructures degrade Rydberg excitation. Understanding and mitigating these charges is crucial for practical devices.
method: Laser-cooled Rb atoms are excited to Rydberg states via the evanescent field of an optical nanofiber while red- and blue-detuned dipole trapping fields are applied. The Rydberg excitation spectrum is measured over time, and an external oscillating electric field is used to suppress spectral features. A model incorporating DC Stark shifts from surface charges reproduces the observations.
result: Time-dependent spectral features appear when dipole trapping fields are on, which are suppressed by an oscillating electric field, indicating surface charge accumulation. Collisional ionization between Rydberg and ground-state atoms, enhanced by trapping fields, is identified as the dominant charge generation mechanism.
conclusion: The results provide insight into charge dynamics at dielectric nanophotonic interfaces and establish practical guidelines for mitigating surface charge-induced electric fields in fiber-integrated Rydberg quantum systems.
