abstract: ArXiv:2607.00256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hypergraphs encode rich multiway interactions, but not all structural information is equally accessible through the dynamics. By analyzing pattern-forming instabilities in reaction-diffusion systems on directed hypergraphs, this work develops a theory of structural visibility that characterizes which features of higher-order structure survive successive levels of dynamical reduction. It is established that higher-order structure is not automatically dynamically relevant. Linearization destroys most higher-order information. Meanwhile, nonlinear reduction recovers only specific higher-order marginals of the adjacency tensor, and projection along critical directions further filters what is dynamically visible. First, we show that the linearized dynamics depends on the hypergraph only through its first-tail-moment statistics, termed exposure. Consequently, exposure-equivalent hypergraphs are linearly indistinguishable in the sense that they exhibit identical dispersion relations and instability thresholds. Next, we define a hierarchy of hyperedge tail-moments that captures progressively detailed co-occurence, and we prove a structural decomposition theorem describing how contractions of these tensors, termed packing effects, influence the reduced amplitude dynamics. This leads to a visibility hierarchy in which successive asymptotic orders reveal increasingly richer structural information. More specifically, exposure governs linear onset while packing effects control post-onset dynamics. Finally, we establish results on nonlinear distinguishability, characterizing when linearly indistinguishable higher-order systems may exhibit different post-onset behaviors. In addition, we formalize when higher-order systems become dynamically indistinguishable from pairwise systems, leading to the notion of dynamical graph surrogacy. Numerical simulations support the theoretical predictions.
tldr: This paper studies structural visibility in reaction-diffusion systems on directed hypergraphs, focusing on pattern formation and dynamical reduction.
motivation: To understand which features of higher-order hypergraph structure are dynamically relevant in pattern-forming systems.
method: Analyzes linear and nonlinear dynamics of reaction-diffusion systems on directed hypergraphs, introducing exposure and packing effects to characterize structural visibility.
result: Linearized dynamics depends only on first-tail-moment statistics (exposure); nonlinear reduction recovers higher-order marginals; a visibility hierarchy emerges where successive orders reveal more structural information.
conclusion: Higher-order structure is not automatically dynamically relevant; linearization destroys most higher-order information, but nonlinear dynamics can recover some, leading to conditions for dynamical graph surrogacy.

title: Rigorous Analysis Of The Time-splitting Methods For The Semiclassical Dirac Equation
authors: Jia Yin He Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide rigorous error analysis of the mass-preserving time-splitting methods for solving the semiclassical Dirac equation. The scaled Planck constant [MATH] in the equation gives rise to rapid oscillations in both space and time when [MATH] with wavelengths of order [MATH]. %We prove that the first-order splitting [MATH] and the second-order splitting [MATH] schemes preserve the total discretized mass. Rigorous error estimates reveal the precise dependence of the approximation errors on the time step [MATH], the spatial mesh size [MATH], and the parameter [MATH]. Specifically, the temporal error scales as [MATH] for the first-order splitting [MATH] and as [MATH] for the second-order splitting [MATH], while the spatial error scales as [MATH] for both methods, where [MATH] is related to the regularity of the solution. In addition, we obtain error bounds for key physical observables, including the total probability density [MATH] and the current density [MATH]. Compared with finite difference time domain (FDTD) methods, time-splitting approaches exhibit spectral accuracy in space and retain a relatively low computational cost. Furthermore, we demonstrate that higher accuracy can be achieved by employing the fourth-order compact time-splitting ([MATH]) method. Numerical experiments are conducted to verify the reliability of the error estimates.
tldr: This paper provides rigorous error analysis of time-splitting methods for the semiclassical Dirac equation, focusing on numerical analysis rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The semiclassical Dirac equation involves rapid oscillations due to the small Planck constant, making numerical simulation challenging. The authors aim to provide rigorous error bounds for time-splitting methods.
method: The authors analyze first-order, second-order, and fourth-order compact time-splitting schemes, proving mass preservation and deriving error estimates that depend on time step, spatial mesh size, and the Planck constant.
result: Temporal error scales as O(Δt) for first-order and O(Δt^2) for second-order splitting; spatial error scales as O(h^m) where m depends on solution regularity. The methods achieve spectral accuracy in space and lower computational cost compared to FDTD.
conclusion: Time-splitting methods are efficient and accurate for the semiclassical Dirac equation, with rigorous error bounds that guide practical discretization choices.

title: Performance Evaluation Of A Certain Transceiver Architecture For Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Phase-Modulated Channels
authors: Hengyu Cui, Ru-Han Chen, Zhenyao He, Shijun Zhu, Ruoqi Sun, Yeqin Tai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels with phase modulation, we recently proposed a method of unitarily transforming the channel matrix into a certain row-echelon form, by which the original MIMO channel can be converted into a certain number of scalar sub-channels with two phase inputs, thereby forming an annulus constellation geometry, and corrupted by both the additive white Gaussian noise and weak self-interference. In this paper, several bounds are derived to evaluate the fundamental limit of such a specific transceiver architecture. Two upper bounds are obtained by upper-bounding the capacity of a scalar channel with an annulus support constraint from the perspective of the convex geometry, while a lower bound is obtained by the standard entropy power inequality. Numerical results show that the gaps between these bounds are small at high signal-to-noise ratios for the MIMO phase-modulated channels over the Rayleigh fading and the single-input multiple-output symbiotic communication system assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface.
tldr: This paper evaluates a transceiver architecture for MIMO phase-modulated channels using convex geometry and entropy power inequality.
motivation: To derive bounds on the capacity of a specific MIMO transceiver architecture with phase modulation.
method: Upper bounds via convex geometry and lower bound via entropy power inequality.
result: Gaps between bounds are small at high SNR for Rayleigh fading and RIS-assisted SIMO systems.
conclusion: The proposed architecture shows promise for MIMO phase-modulated channels.

title: Effective Dynamics Of The Sinkhorn Algorithm In The Regime Of Low Entropy Regularization
authors: Guillaume Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Sinkhorn algorithm is the de facto standard method for numerically solving entropy-regularized optimal transport problems over finite sets. In this work, we investigate a phenomenon arising when Sinkhorn is applied with a small regularization parameter [MATH]: the evolution of the dual variables (the logarithm of the scaling factors) is approximately piecewise-linear, while the primal variables (the approximate transport plans) exhibit a saddle-to-saddle type behavior. We prove that as [MATH], the Sinkhorn iterates indeed converge to a continuous-time curve consistent with these observations, when time is rescaled as [MATH], and we characterize the limiting "cold Sinkhorn" dynamics explicitly. In particular, we show that it acts as a dual optimization dynamics for the unregularized problem with properties analogous to the simplex algorithm. Notably, this dynamics converges in finite time to an unregularized solution, implying a novel guarantee for the Sinkhorn algorithm itself: it achieves [MATH] dual suboptimality in [MATH] iterations, instead of [MATH] as existing analyses would suggest.
tldr: This paper analyzes the dynamics of the Sinkhorn algorithm for entropy-regularized optimal transport in the low-regularization regime, showing convergence to a piecewise-linear curve and finite-time convergence to an unregularized solution.
motivation: The Sinkhorn algorithm is widely used for optimal transport, but its behavior under small regularization is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize the dynamics and prove convergence guarantees.
method: The authors study the continuous-time limit of the Sinkhorn iterations as the regularization parameter goes to zero, rescaling time appropriately, and derive explicit limiting dynamics.
result: They prove that the iterates converge to a continuous-time curve with piecewise-linear dual variables and saddle-to-saddle primal behavior, and that the limiting dynamics converges in finite time to an unregularized solution, implying an improved iteration complexity bound.
conclusion: The work provides a novel theoretical understanding of the Sinkhorn algorithm in the low-regularization regime, with implications for optimal transport computation.

title: Bayesian Updates From Coalgebraic Determinisation
authors: Nathaniel Virgo Manuel Baltieri
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The powerset construction is the classical determinisation procedure for nondeterministic finite automata. In the coalgebraic setting, this construction has been generalised to structured coalgebras, which are coalgebras equipped with extra data. For stochastic Moore machines over the distribution monad, a type of structured coalgebra, the determinisation construction induces a semantics assigning to each finite input word a distribution on the current output. This semantics is appropriate when only the current output matters, but it is too coarse for settings in which intermediate observations must also be taken into account, as is typical for agents solving POMDPs in control theory and reinforcement learning. In these contexts, agents need to condition on all realised observations, not just the final one, so to better plan for the future. This has been addressed from a category theoretic perspective through a procedure called ``unifilarisation'', which (in our context) takes a stochastic Mealy machine and produces a machine whose states are priors over the original state space and whose transitions are given by Bayesian filtering. Here we show that unifilarisation is an instance of coalgebraic determinisation. We work with Mealy machines over monads equipped with extra structure generalising the notion of the support of a distribution. We show that in this setting, unifilarisation arises from the general determinisation procedure. We then compare the resulting final coalgebra semantics with the Moore-style one. Instead of assigning only a distribution on current outputs to each finite input word, it yields causal stochastic behaviours, that is, families mapping input words to distributions on output words compatible with the ``causality'' constraint that outputs cannot depend on future inputs.
tldr: The paper presents a coalgebraic framework for unifilarisation of stochastic Mealy machines, showing it as an instance of determinisation.
motivation: To provide a categorical semantics for agents that condition on all observations, as needed in control theory and reinforcement learning, which is not captured by Moore-style semantics.
method: The authors work with Mealy machines over monads with extra structure generalising support of a distribution, and show that unifilarisation arises from the general coalgebraic determinisation procedure.
result: Unifilarisation yields causal stochastic behaviours, mapping input words to distributions on output words respecting causality, rather than just distributions on current outputs.
conclusion: The coalgebraic perspective unifies determinisation and unifilarisation, offering a principled semantics for sequential decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Scalable Security And Migration-Aware Sfc Provisioning In Leo Satellite Networks
authors: Mohammed Mahyoub, Wael Jaafar, Sami Muhaidat, Halim Yanikomeroglu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are emerging as a backbone for global 6G connectivity, where independent tenant slices share orbital infrastructure, each requiring an ordered chain of security virtual network functions (VNFs). Because onboard computation and networking are scarce, slices cannot be given dedicated VNFs. They must share instances on the same satellites, enlarging the attack surface and exposing tenants to cross-slice side-channel risk. This exposure shifts continually as visibility, orbital motion, and the inter-satellite topology change in time (epochs), making VNF migration a structural necessity that couples resource efficiency, service continuity, and security isolation into a single problem. We formulate this security- and migration-aware security function chain (SFC) placement as a multi-slice mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) whose core is a co-location risk model, grounded in ISO/NIST principles and supported by analytic bounds, in which we separate avoidable migrations from those forced by orbital motion. Because the joint program scales quadratically with the cross-slice co-location terms, we develop an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)-inspired penalized per-slice best response decomposition that recasts the coupling as a linear per-slice penalty, yielding independent subproblems through sequential (S-ADMM) and parallel, collision-repaired (P-ADMM) schedules. Simulations over a Walker-Delta satellite constellation show that the proposed framework eliminates co-location risk, reduces SFC migrations, and sustains full delay compliance, while remaining feasible within the per-epoch budget for slice counts where the monolithic security-aware MILP is intractable.
tldr: This paper proposes a security- and migration-aware SFC placement framework for LEO satellite networks using MILP and ADMM-based decomposition.
motivation: LEO satellite networks face challenges in securely provisioning virtual network functions for multiple tenants due to limited onboard resources and dynamic orbital motion, which necessitates VNF migration and risk-aware placement.
method: The authors formulate a multi-slice MILP with a co-location risk model and develop an ADMM-inspired penalized per-slice best response decomposition (S-ADMM and P-ADMM) to solve the problem efficiently.
result: Simulations show the framework eliminates co-location risk, reduces SFC migrations, and maintains delay compliance while being scalable for larger slice counts compared to the monolithic MILP.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively addresses security and migration challenges in LEO satellite SFC provisioning, enabling feasible and scalable deployment.

title: QuaMoE-DRF: Proactive Beam And Rate Adaptation Via Multimodal Dynamic Radio Map Forecasting In Isac Networks
authors: Zhihan Zeng, Kaihe Wang, Zhongpei Zhang, Chongwen Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static radio maps provide location-dependent propagation priors, but they cannot capture short-term blockage caused by moving objects. Direct sensing-assisted beam prediction is also limited because a beam index discards SINR margins, MCS thresholds, BS alternatives, and communication-equivalent neighboring beams. This paper proposes QuaMoE-DRF, a quality-aware multimodal dynamic radio map forecasting framework for proactive beam and rate adaptation in ISAC networks. Its core representation is a future beam-SINR field. We show that the full multi-BS beam-SINR field is sufficient for finite-codebook threshold-rate BS, beam, MCS, goodput, and outage decisions. For tractability, the implemented model learns a compact reference-BS local field, complemented by BS-level supervision, joint BS--beam supervision, and latent network context; we also clarify that this compact projection alone is not sufficient for BS association. QuaMoE-DRF fuses static geometry, event-like motion observations, structured sensing states, and wireless history through a quality-aware mixture-of-experts module motivated by inverse-variance fusion under heteroscedastic modality errors. It jointly predicts communication-oriented map channels and proactive BS, beam, and MCS decisions. On a dynamic multi-BS and multi-UE urban benchmark, QuaMoE-DRF achieves 402.5 Mbps effective rate, 0.0417 outage probability, and 0.1836 map RMSE, improving the effective rate by 5.67% and reducing outage by 8.35% over the strongest completed effective-rate baseline. The current validation uses labels from a compact blockage/path-loss simulator, with ray tracing used only for calibration and sanity checking.
tldr: This paper proposes a multimodal dynamic radio map forecasting framework for proactive beam and rate adaptation in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks.
motivation: Static radio maps cannot capture short-term blockages, and direct sensing-assisted beam prediction lacks SINR margins and other communication metrics.
method: The framework uses a quality-aware mixture-of-experts module to fuse static geometry, motion observations, sensing states, and wireless history, predicting future beam-SINR fields and proactive BS/beam/MCS decisions.
result: On a dynamic multi-BS multi-UE urban benchmark, the method achieves 402.5 Mbps effective rate, 0.0417 outage probability, and 0.1836 map RMSE, improving effective rate by 5.67% and reducing outage by 8.35% over baselines.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively combines sensing and communication for proactive resource allocation in ISAC networks.

title: Toward A Unified Security And Privacy Framework For AI-Native 6g Networks
authors: Bidushi Barua, Ahsan Khan, Kangfeng Ye, Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Yifan Liu, Mohit Bidikar, Anthony Moulds, Julie Mccann, Poonam Yadav
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sixth Generation (6G) communication networks are expected to evolve into AI-native, highly autonomous ecosystems that integrate communication, computing, sensing, and artificial intelligence. While these capabilities enable unprecedented connectivity and intelligent services, they also create a highly heterogeneous security and privacy landscape that cannot be addressed through isolated, technology-specific solutions. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of security and privacy in AI-native 6G networks from a cross-layer perspective. We first examine the fragmentation of existing security and privacy approaches across emerging technologies, network architectures, AI systems, and standardization efforts, motivating the need for a unified security and privacy framework. Building upon this framework, we develop a cross-layer threat taxonomy encompassing infrastructure, network and architectural, AI, privacy, and security management domains, and analyze representative threats across key AI-native 6G technologies. Furthermore, we map these threats to corresponding cross-layer countermeasures, including standards harmonization as a security function, and identify critical research gaps and future priorities for secure, interoperable, and trustworthy AI-native 6G ecosystems. Finally, we discuss future research directions toward realizing secure, privacy-preserving, resilient, and globally interoperable 6G networks. This survey provides researchers, practitioners, and standardization communities with a holistic foundation for the design, evaluation, and deployment of trustworthy AI-native 6G systems.
tldr: A survey on security and privacy challenges in AI-native 6G networks, proposing a cross-layer unified framework.
motivation: Existing security approaches for 6G are fragmented across technologies, architectures, and AI systems, lacking a holistic solution.
method: The paper conducts a comprehensive survey, develops a cross-layer threat taxonomy, and maps threats to countermeasures.
result: Identifies critical research gaps and future priorities for secure, interoperable, and trustworthy AI-native 6G ecosystems.
conclusion: A unified security and privacy framework is essential for the design and deployment of trustworthy AI-native 6G networks.

conclusion: Incorporating group-level behavioral responses is essential for accurately modeling and controlling contagion processes in social networks.

result: Obtains analytical expressions for mean squared displacement and effective diffusion coefficient as functions of chirality and noise parameters.
conclusion: The theory captures the interplay between chirality and density fluctuations, providing insights into active matter transport.

tldr: This paper studies how quorum sensing in bacterial communities promotes antifragility and increases diversity, using a computational model.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition is important for ecology and evolution of microbial communities.
method: The authors develop a computational model of bacterial communities with quorum sensing and analyze the emergence of antifragile regimes and diversity.
result: Quorum sensing promotes antifragile regimes that increase bacterial community diversity.
conclusion: Quorum sensing can lead to more robust and diverse bacterial communities through antifragile dynamics.

conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of stochastic processes in traffic flow but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064149] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic search with space-dependent diffusivity, a problem in statistical physics and applied mathematics.
motivation: Understanding how a diffusing searcher finds a target in heterogeneous environments is important for many applications, but exact solutions are rare.
method: The authors analyze a model where the diffusivity varies with position, deriving exact results for certain cases and using asymptotic analysis.
result: They obtain explicit formulas for mean first-passage times and splitting probabilities, revealing how spatial variations in diffusivity affect search efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides new analytical insights into stochastic search in heterogeneous media, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall are performed to compute first-passage-time statistics.
result: Wall-induced hindered diffusion delays wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction leads to distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion significantly affect the first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near walls, with implications for microbial ecology and biophysics.

authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experimental observations, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment leads to novel phenomena such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with broad implications for various fields.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on magnetoelastic coupling.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic phases in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice contraction and dramatic stiffening of the lattice.
conclusion: The magnetic order becomes locked to the lattice, possibly due to Fermi surface nesting, suggesting strong magnetoelastic coupling in frustrated magnets.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for computing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills theory.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: Identifies a hidden 10d conformal symmetry and obtains the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel operators.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

title: Demodulating Digital Holograms With Unknown Uniform Phase-shifts By Spiral Phase Transform
authors: Pavel Trochtchanovitch
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Spiral Phase Transform (SPT) is a generalization of the Hilbert transform for 2D signals and, as such, can be used for AC signal demodulation. However, phase demodulation with the SPT is complicated by a multiplicative term that depends on the fringe directional map. We derived an analytical formula for the twofold directional map and applied the SPT for the blind reconstruction of phase-shifted digital holograms. Possible phase ambiguities in the unfolded directional map were resolved by satisfying the spatial uniformity condition of the phase shifts. The method was experimentally verified using on-axis and off-axis digital holograms of specularly reflecting subjects.
tldr: This paper presents a method for demodulating digital holograms with unknown uniform phase shifts using the Spiral Phase Transform.
motivation: Phase demodulation in digital holography is complicated by a multiplicative term depending on the fringe directional map; the authors aim to derive an analytical formula for the twofold directional map to enable blind reconstruction.
method: The authors derive an analytical formula for the twofold directional map and apply the Spiral Phase Transform (SPT) to demodulate phase-shifted digital holograms, resolving phase ambiguities by enforcing spatial uniformity of phase shifts.
result: The method is experimentally verified using on-axis and off-axis digital holograms of specularly reflecting subjects, demonstrating successful blind reconstruction.
conclusion: The proposed SPT-based approach effectively demodulates digital holograms with unknown uniform phase shifts, providing a practical solution for holographic imaging.

title: Correct Asymptotic Wavefunctions For Calculating Photoelectron Angular Distributions Of O2- And No-
authors: Wenru Jie, Rui Zhang, Jiayi Chen, Qihan Liu, Chuangang Ning
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ab initio calculation of photoelectron angular distributions (PADs) for negative ions remains a significant theoretical challenge. In this work, we report a joint experimental and theoretical investigation of PADs for a series of molecular anions with varying polarities, including the nonpolar O2-, the weakly polar NO-, and the strongly polar AsO- and SbO-. To accurately describe the long-range electronic wavefunctions -- where photodetachment contributes most strongly -- we modified the standard Gaussian-type orbitals (GTOs) by augmenting them with a correct exponential Slater-tail basis set (~e^(-{\xi}r)). This simple yet effective approach significantly improves the agreement between the experimental and theoretical PADs for O2- and NO-. However, notable discrepancies persist for NO- for transitions to the v = 0 and v = 1 vibrational levels of neutral NO even after this correction. Given that our methodology successfully reproduced PADs for strongly polar anions (e.g., AsO- and SbO-), these residual discrepancies are unlikely to stem from "exit-channel scattering" induced by long-range dipole fields. Instead, we tentatively attribute the failure for NO- to the breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation or the frozen orbital approximation, arising from the extremely weak binding of the excess electron.
tldr: This paper presents a joint experimental and theoretical study of photoelectron angular distributions for molecular anions, focusing on improving wavefunction accuracy with Slater-type orbitals.
motivation: Accurate calculation of photoelectron angular distributions for negative ions is a significant theoretical challenge, and existing methods fail for certain molecules.
method: The authors modified standard Gaussian-type orbitals by adding an exponential Slater-tail basis set to better describe long-range wavefunctions, and compared theoretical predictions with experimental measurements for O2-, NO-, AsO-, and SbO-.
result: The modified basis set significantly improved agreement for O2- and NO-, but discrepancies remained for NO- transitions to v=0 and v=1, while strongly polar anions were well described.
conclusion: The residual discrepancies for NO- are tentatively attributed to breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation or frozen orbital approximation due to extremely weak electron binding.

Excellent agreement is found with results reported in the literature. Simple and useful approximate formulas to treat the nuclear-size correction are obtained, which, in particular, can be used to study the self-energy contributions to the field-shift factors.
tldr: This paper calculates nuclear-size corrections to one-loop self-energy in hydrogenlike ions within QED.
motivation: Accurate QED calculations are needed for high-precision spectroscopy of highly charged ions, but nuclear-size effects on self-energy are not fully understood.
method: The authors perform nonperturbative QED calculations for various nuclear charges and states, obtaining diagonal and off-diagonal matrix elements.
result: They find excellent agreement with literature and provide simple approximate formulas for the nuclear-size correction.
conclusion: The results and formulas can be used to study self-energy contributions to field-shift factors in hydrogenlike ions.

title: Nondipole Contributions To Attosecond Chiral Photoionization Asymmetries
authors: Zheming Zhou, Yang Li, Yueming Zhou, Peixiang Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoelectron circular dichroism (PECD) reads molecular chirality from forward-backward asymmetries in photoelectron emission, but the same observable can also contain non-dipole contributions from photon momentum transfer. Here we show that such contributions can reshape attosecond PECD measurements in both one- and two-photon ionization of chiral molecules. Calculations beyond the dipole approximation, interpreted with perturbation theory, reveal that non-dipole effects modify not only the magnitude but also the phase of the emitted electron wave packet. In two-photon interferometry, pathway interference amplifies the non-dipole response and can reverse the apparent chiral asymmetry. We further identify a practical separation principle: the non-dipole component is insensitive to enantiomeric handedness and can therefore be obtained from a racemic mixture. Subtracting this background isolates the purely chirality-induced asymmetry, enabling more accurate measurements of chiral electron dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies nondipole contributions to attosecond chiral photoionization asymmetries, focusing on photoelectron circular dichroism in chiral molecules.
motivation: Understanding chiral electron dynamics is important for molecular physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use calculations beyond the dipole approximation and perturbation theory to analyze one- and two-photon ionization of chiral molecules.
result: Non-dipole effects modify the magnitude and phase of the emitted electron wave packet, and in two-photon interferometry they can reverse the apparent chiral asymmetry.
conclusion: The non-dipole component is insensitive to enantiomeric handedness and can be subtracted using racemic mixtures to isolate purely chirality-induced asymmetry.

title: Active Sensing For RIS-Aided Tracking And Power Control: A Hybrid Neuroevolution And Supervised Learning Approach
authors: George Stamatelis, Hui Chen, Henk Henk Wymeersch, George C. Alexandropoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies energy efficient tracking of power-limited mobile users with the assistance of a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS). Since localization pilot transmissions dominate the energy budget of power-constrained devices, we introduce a low-overhead feedback link from the Base Station (BS) to the user to enable dynamic uplink power control. To navigate the discrete and decentralized nature of this active sensing problem, we propose a novel Dual-Agent (DA) deep learning framework that jointly optimizes the discrete RIS phase profiles and the UE's transmit power in real time. Specifically, our approach employs a hybrid training methodology integrating the neuroevolution paradigm with supervised learning, effectively overcoming the non-differentiability of discrete phase responses from the RIS unit elements and the strict information bottleneck of single-bit feedback messages for pilot power control. The proposed DA active sensing framework can be applied with both single- and multi-antenna BSs, the latter with only minor modifications in the structure of one NN: an additional output branch with appropriate structure is included for the latter case to select a valid digital combiner from a finite set. Extensive numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves highly accurate and robust tracking across diverse target motion models, outperforming extended Kalman and particle filters, as well as, machine learning-based trackers. Furthermore, in static localization, it is shown to significantly outperform traditional fingerprinting schemes, deep reinforcement learning baselines, and standard backpropagation-based estimators.
tldr: This paper proposes a dual-agent deep learning framework for RIS-aided tracking and power control, using neuroevolution and supervised learning.
motivation: To enable energy-efficient tracking of power-limited mobile users with RIS assistance, addressing the challenge of discrete RIS phase optimization and single-bit feedback.
method: A hybrid training methodology combining neuroevolution and supervised learning is used to jointly optimize RIS phase profiles and user transmit power in real time.
result: The proposed scheme achieves highly accurate and robust tracking across diverse motion models, outperforming Kalman filters and other ML-based trackers.
conclusion: The dual-agent active sensing framework is effective for RIS-aided localization and tracking, with potential for static localization as well.

title: A Short Review Of Estimators For The Glm Predictive Of Laplace Bayesian Neural Networks
authors: Romie Banerjee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This short review examines the primary approaches for estimating the predictive distribution of Laplace-approximated Bayesian neural networks, with particular focus on the Generalized Linear Model (GLM) formulation. We survey the landscape of estimation strategies, from exact GLM computations requiring full Jacobian evaluations to Monte Carlo approximations that trade computational cost for statistical efficiency. The review covers the theoretical foundations of the Laplace approximation, the Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (KFAC) method for scalable posterior inference, and the various predictive estimation techniques developed in the literature. We provide a unified presentation that clarifies the relationships between methods and highlights their respective computational and statistical trade-offs.
tldr: A review of predictive estimation methods for Laplace-approximated Bayesian neural networks, focusing on GLM formulations.
motivation: To provide a unified overview of estimation strategies for the predictive distribution of Laplace-approximated Bayesian neural networks, highlighting computational and statistical trade-offs.
method: The paper surveys exact GLM computations, Monte Carlo approximations, and Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (KFAC) methods, presenting a unified framework.
result: The review clarifies relationships between different estimation techniques and their respective trade-offs.
conclusion: The paper serves as a reference for practitioners choosing predictive estimation methods for Bayesian neural networks.

title: WarpagePINN: Thermal Warpage Prediction In Advanced Packaging Via A Two-Stage Physics-Informed Neural Networks
authors: Xinyu Li, Min Tang, Zeyu Sun, Wenxing Zhu, Jianhua Zhang, Liang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal warpage has become a critical issue in advanced packaging, primarily caused by the mismatch in coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) among heterogeneously integrated materials. However, only a limited number of studies have focused on developing computational methods for coupled thermal-warpage prediction in the chiplet. This paper proposes a two-stage physics-informed neural network (WarpagePINN) framework to compute both temperature profile and warpage deformation of chiplets. The neural networks are trained without relying on labeled datasets generated by conventional simulators. In the first stage, the temperature field is modeled using a Fourier series representation that inherently satisfies boundary conditions, and the network is trained solely through a loss function derived from the governing equation. In the second stage, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) is employed for warpage prediction, utilizing a novel hybrid supervisory strategy to optimize the energy-based loss function instead of residual loss. A parametric WarpagePINN is also developed to quantify uncertainties associated with the CTE. Numerical results show that the proposed WarpagePINN framework achieves excellent agreement with conventional finite element methods, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.2 {\mu}m, while achieving a speedup of approximately 1000 {\times} in CTE parameterization studies.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to predict thermal warpage in advanced packaging, a topic unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Thermal warpage due to CTE mismatch is a critical issue in chiplet packaging, but existing computational methods are limited.
method: A two-stage PINN framework first models temperature field with Fourier series, then predicts warpage using an MLP with energy-based loss.
result: The method achieves 0.2 μm MAE compared to FEM and 1000× speedup in CTE parameterization studies.
conclusion: WarpagePINN provides an efficient and accurate alternative to FEM for thermal warpage prediction.

title: Physics Informed Neural Networks For Nonlinear Delay Differential Equations
authors: Stone Yao, Vipin Kumar, Roberto Guglielmi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we propose a novel physics-informed neural network framework for solving general first-order delay differential equations. Our approach combines a differentiable history switch, a trial-solution formulation that explicitly enforces history constraints, and a segmented collocation strategy to stabilize gradient propagation across large temporal domains. The method enables a scalable and physics-consistent approximation of delay differential equation solutions while maintaining continuity across subintervals. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes a physics-informed neural network framework for solving nonlinear delay differential equations.
motivation: Delay differential equations are challenging to solve numerically, and existing methods may struggle with stability and accuracy over long time domains.
method: The method combines a differentiable history switch, a trial-solution formulation that enforces history constraints, and a segmented collocation strategy to stabilize gradient propagation.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in approximating solutions of delay differential equations.
conclusion: The proposed PINN framework provides a scalable and physics-consistent approach for solving delay differential equations.

title: A Multilevel Stochastic-gradient Neural Solver For Boundary Integral Equations
authors: Richard Tsai Bing-Ze Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a multilevel stochastic-gradient neural solver for boundary integral equations of the second kind. The unknown density is represented by a multilayer perceptron, trained by minimizing the Nystr\"om-discretized residual on a ladder of refining quadrature grids, each level warm-started from the parameters of the previous one. Each step requires only dense matrix-vector products on mini-batches of collocation rows and network passes, operations that map directly onto GPU hardware. The residual contraction is governed by the empirical neural tangent kernel (NTK), the discrete sample of a single continuum kernel. On a fixed grid, training stalls once the residual concentrates in modes the network contracts slowly, the plateau described by the frequency principle; a spectral analysis explains, and experiments confirm, how refining the quadrature resolves more of the continuum kernel's spectrum and returns these modes to the optimizer's reach. Spectral bias, elsewhere an obstruction to neural network solvers, thus serves as the smoother of a multigrid-type iteration, with quadrature refinement in place of coarse-grid correction. Under a uniform regularity bound on the network, the total work is a constant multiple of the work on the finest grid, and the uniform conditioning of the discrete second-kind operator leaves the NTK as the sole rate-determining spectrum while converting the training residual into an a posteriori error bound. Experiments on interior Dirichlet Laplace/Poisson problems and exterior Neumann Helmholtz problems, using both parametric and signed-distance surface representations, demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared with GMRES at comparable tolerances.
tldr: A multilevel stochastic-gradient neural solver for boundary integral equations using a multilayer perceptron and Nyström discretization.
motivation: To develop an efficient neural solver for boundary integral equations that leverages GPU hardware and overcomes spectral bias via multigrid-like refinement.
method: The unknown density is represented by a multilayer perceptron trained by minimizing the Nyström-discretized residual on a hierarchy of refining quadrature grids, with each level warm-started from the previous one.
result: The method achieves residual contraction governed by the neural tangent kernel, and quadrature refinement resolves spectral bias, enabling efficient solution of Laplace/Poisson and Helmholtz problems.
conclusion: The proposed solver is effective and efficient compared to GMRES, with total work a constant multiple of the finest grid work.

title: Vehicle Routing Problem Meets Large Language Models: An Overview And Perspectives
authors: Xianchao Xiu, Chong Shen, Yanjiao Zhu, Wanquan Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The vehicle routing problem (VRP) is a central optimization problem in artificial intelligence, logistics automation, transportation scheduling, and industrial decision-making. VRP and its variants are NP-hard, and practical routing tasks often combine time windows, vehicle capacities, pickup-and-delivery relations, dynamic requests, and other operational constraints, making both modeling and solving difficult. Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for routing optimization by processing natural-language requirements, generating code, reasoning over constraints, and interacting with external tools. This survey reviews LLM-driven research on VRP, covering the basic definition, main variants, major solver families, and LLM concepts needed for this topic. Existing studies are organized into three roles: modelers translate natural-language requirements into constraints and modeling code; designers generate heuristics, operators, or route plans; and coordinators organize tool calls, multi-agent collaboration, and connections with neural solvers. The survey also reviews standard benchmarks, real or near-real operational datasets, LLM-oriented evaluation frameworks, and two comparative experiments. The goal is to clarify current progress in LLM-assisted routing optimization and provide a structured reference for intelligent decision-making, advanced manufacturing, and industrial automation.
tldr: A survey on using large language models to assist vehicle routing problem optimization.
motivation: Vehicle routing problems are NP-hard and complex; LLMs offer a flexible interface for modeling and solving them.
method: Reviews LLM-driven approaches categorized as modelers, designers, and coordinators, and evaluates benchmarks and experiments.
result: Identifies current progress and structured roles of LLMs in routing optimization.
conclusion: LLMs show promise for VRP but the field is nascent; the survey provides a reference for future work.

title: Federated Sovereign Transport Protocol (fstp): Verifiable Coordination Without Disclosure
authors: Ram\'on Soto C. (department Of Accounting, University Of Sonora), Liz Soto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces the Federated Sovereign Transport Protocol (FSTP), a synchronization boundary and transport layer for federated networks in which nodes have heterogeneous privacy requirements. Existing federation protocols leave data confinement to operator policy: they define message formats and delivery semantics but impose no structural constraint on what a conforming server may emit. FSTP addresses this gap by making data confinement a property of the protocol itself. The central mechanism is a synchronization agent whose output type set is formally closed. Raw internal data cannot appear in any federation message because the constraint is enforced by the Rust type system at compile time, not by a runtime check. A contextual identity model derives a separate, unlinkable identifier for each federation relationship, preventing cross-context correlation structurally. A Blocklace-based event substrate provides tamper-evident, partially ordered logging with synchronization cost proportional to the symmetric difference between node states, and supports data erasure without breaking the hash chain. The result is proof without exposure: a federation participant can verify that a process occurred, that a credential is authentic, and that an outcome is uncorrupted without accessing the internal data that produced these artifacts. FSTP is developed as the inter-node transport layer of Velyzor, a governance platform for institutions with demanding confidentiality requirements. The specification and reference implementation are released as open-source infrastructure under Apache 2.0; source code and figures accompany this paper.
tldr: This paper introduces a federated network protocol that enforces data confinement and contextual identity through compile-time type system constraints.
motivation: Existing federation protocols rely on operator policy for data confinement, which is insufficient for heterogeneous privacy requirements.
method: The protocol uses a synchronization agent with a formally closed output type set enforced by the Rust type system, a contextual identity model for unlinkable identifiers, and a Blocklace-based event substrate for tamper-evident logging.
result: The protocol achieves proof without exposure, allowing verification of processes and credentials without revealing internal data.
conclusion: FSTP provides a structural solution to data confinement in federated networks, with a reference implementation released as open-source.

title: Feasibilism, Explication, And The Cobham-Edmonds Thesis
authors: Abrahim Ladha, Yiran Luo, Alan Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While the Church-Turing thesis asserts that effective calculability explicates to sets decidable by a Turing machine, the Cobham-Edmonds thesis asserts that feasible computation explicates to the complexity class [MATH], those decidable by a polynomial-time bounded Turing machine. The Church-Turing thesis has been placed under rigorous scrutiny and has several convincing arguments in its favor, but the Cobham-Edmonds thesis has not undergone a similar examination. Many of the arguments in its favor simply suggest that [MATH] is a useful assumption, rather than a necessary target. This paper presents analogous arguments in favor of the Cobham-Edmonds thesis.
tldr: The paper discusses the Cobham-Edmonds thesis that feasible computation corresponds to polynomial-time Turing machines, presenting arguments in its favor.
motivation: The Cobham-Edmonds thesis lacks rigorous scrutiny compared to the Church-Turing thesis; the authors aim to provide analogous arguments to support it.
method: The paper presents philosophical and logical arguments analogous to those supporting the Church-Turing thesis, analyzing the concept of feasible computation and its explication to P.
result: The paper offers a set of arguments that suggest P is a necessary target for feasible computation, not merely a useful assumption.
conclusion: The Cobham-Edmonds thesis can be supported by arguments similar to those for the Church-Turing thesis, strengthening its philosophical foundation.

title: Multiwinner Voting With Spatial Preferences Under Incomplete Information
authors: Drew Springham, Edith Elkind, Bart de Keijzer, Maria Polukarov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In multiwinner elections with many candidates, as in participatory budgeting or large-scale recommendation, voters cannot plausibly evaluate every candidate, yet standard proportional-fairness guarantees such as EJR+ are stated for fully specified approval ballots. We ask whether strong proportional representation can still be guaranteed while eliciting only a little from each voter. We study this in a spatial model, the Axis-aligned Random Rectangle Voter (ARRV) model, in which candidates occupy a [MATH]-dimensional issue space and each voter approves an axis-aligned hyper-rectangle: a tolerance interval on every issue. Preferences are revealed only through Planar queries, each comparing a voter's tolerance to a candidate on a single issue. We give an algorithm returning an EJR+ committee for any distribution over rectangular preferences, using only [MATH] Planar queries per voter in expectation given a sufficiently large electorate, independent of the number of candidates [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of issues and [MATH] the committee size. The algorithm rests on a dimension-agnostic verify-or-fallback framework whose query cost is governed by two properties supplied by interchangeable modules. We describe such modules, yielding end-to-end guarantees for known, unknown, and smooth distributions.
tldr: This paper studies multiwinner voting with spatial preferences under incomplete information, focusing on proportional representation guarantees.
motivation: In multiwinner elections with many candidates, voters cannot evaluate all candidates, yet standard fairness guarantees assume fully specified preferences. The authors aim to achieve strong proportional representation with minimal voter input.
method: They propose a spatial model (ARRV) where voters approve axis-aligned hyper-rectangles, and preferences are elicited via Planar queries. An algorithm using a verify-or-fallback framework returns an EJR+ committee with few queries per voter.
result: The algorithm guarantees an EJR+ committee using only O(kd) Planar queries per voter in expectation, independent of the number of candidates, for known, unknown, and smooth distributions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that strong proportional representation can be achieved with limited preference elicitation in a spatial model, offering practical algorithms for large-scale elections.

title: Definability Of Functional Properties In The Basic Modal-Temporal Language Over Ordered Frames
authors: Alfredo Burrieza
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the expressive power of the simplest modal-temporal language, obtained by adding Prior's temporal operators \(G\) and \(H\) to the basic modal language with \(\Box\). This language is the standard bimodal combination of modal and tense logic; under its functional interpretation it is denoted \(L_{T\times W}\). To analyse its definability across five order types, we consider two semantic readings of the temporal operators: the standard reading (\(G,H\)), which includes the current instant, and the strict reading (\(G^{\ast},H^{\ast}\)), which always excludes it. We examine nine functional properties -- totality, non-totality, injectivity, surjectivity, monotonicity, strict monotonicity, antitonicity, strict antitonicity, and constancy -- over preorders, strict preorders, partial orders, linear orders, and strict linear orders. Our analysis reveals two different levels of expressive power. In the original multiflow setting, the language is quite weak and the two readings coincide. When we restrict the semantics to minimal functional frames (the \(O^{2}\) family), many properties become definable, and the choice of reading becomes crucial: the strict reading can define properties such as injectivity even in reflexive orders. The same definability patterns appear with indexed languages and with the Uniform Domain condition on the semantics of \(L_{T\times W}\). That three such different ways of controlling functional multiplicity lead to identical definability patterns indicates that the expressive limitations of the original framework come from the uncontrolled multiplicity of functions, not from any weakness of the operators. Even after controlling functional multiplicity, a set of properties remains undefinable in all non-linear orders, showing that the lack of connectivity is a fundamental obstacle.
tldr: This paper studies the definability of functional properties in a basic modal-temporal language over ordered frames, which is a topic in modal logic and temporal logic.
motivation: To understand the expressive power of a simple modal-temporal language and how different semantic readings and restrictions on frames affect definability of functional properties.
method: The paper analyzes nine functional properties under two semantic readings (standard and strict) over five order types, using minimal functional frames and indexed languages.
result: The language is weak in the original multiflow setting, but many properties become definable when semantics is restricted to minimal functional frames; the strict reading can define injectivity even in reflexive orders.
conclusion: Expressive limitations stem from uncontrolled multiplicity of functions, not operator weakness; lack of connectivity is a fundamental obstacle for definability in non-linear orders.

title: Destination-Labeled Self-Looping Systems With Dwell: Intrinsic Characterization, Realization Cost, And Recognition
authors: Reda Belaiche
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a finite-state symbolic controller for systems in which the admissible visible transitions are fixed in advance and each visible state carries a minimum dwell requirement. The resulting model, which we call a destination-labeled self-looping system with dwell (DLSL system), records the visible graph together with local decision maps; dwell memory appears only after phase expansion. The main structural issue is that, once dwell is imposed, the current visible state no longer determines whether a departure is allowed. This leads to the converse problem: which deterministic transducers arise as phase-expanded realizations of DLSL systems over a fixed visible graph? We show that the answer is exactly the class of fiber-linear graph-respecting transducers. Under natural reachability and realizable-departure assumptions, equivalent accessible realizations over the same visible graph are isomorphic; in particular, the visible transduction determines the dwell vector and the local decision maps. We also prove that any graph-preserving deterministic realization enforcing dwell values [MATH] requires exactly [MATH] control states. Finally, we give an [MATH] recognition and reconstruction procedure, and extend the analysis to an edge-entry variant in which transitions may enter interior phases of successor fibers.
tldr: This paper studies a class of finite-state symbolic controllers with dwell constraints, focusing on their characterization, realization cost, and recognition.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structural properties and realizability of deterministic transducers that arise from destination-labeled self-looping systems with dwell, which are relevant to control theory and formal methods.
method: The paper provides an intrinsic characterization of such systems using fiber-linear graph-respecting transducers, analyzes the minimal number of control states required, and develops a recognition and reconstruction algorithm.
result: It shows that under natural assumptions, equivalent realizations over the same visible graph are isomorphic, and gives an O(n^2) recognition procedure.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of finite-state controllers with dwell, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sample Complexities Of Estimating Gumbel--Max Watermark Proportions With And Without Reduction To Pivotal Statistics
authors: Qiaosen Wang Shuwen Chai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00224v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Watermarking promises a statistical trace of large language model (LLM) use, but real documents, after editing or paraphrasing, rarely arrive as purely human-written or purely machine-generated. This motivates a quantitative question beyond detection: what proportion of a document is generated from a pre-specified watermarked LLM? We study this watermark proportion estimation problem under the Gumbel--max watermarking mechanism, treating the next-token prediction (NTP) distributions as unknown and arbitrary nuisance parameters subject to a non-degeneracy condition. We compare two observation regimes: in the full observation regime, the estimator observes the pseudorandom vector and the selected token at each position; under the more popular setting of pivotal reduction, it observes only a scalar pivot, which follows a one-dimensional Uniform--Beta mixture distribution. Under pivotal reduction, we develop a Laguerre-polynomial estimator and establish a matching information-theoretic lower bound for the sample complexity. For full observation, we introduce an event-counting estimator and show a matching lower bound, yielding a substantially smaller sample complexity. As our results imply, although reducing to pivotal statistics is an elegant and widely used procedure, it is not always sample-efficient for estimating the proportion of watermarks.
tldr: This paper studies the sample complexity of estimating the proportion of watermarked text generated by a Gumbel-max watermarked LLM, comparing full observation and pivotal reduction regimes.
motivation: Real documents often contain mixed human and machine-generated text, so estimating the proportion of watermarked content is important beyond simple detection.
method: The authors develop a Laguerre-polynomial estimator for the pivotal reduction regime and an event-counting estimator for the full observation regime, and derive matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
result: The full observation regime yields substantially smaller sample complexity than the pivotal reduction regime, showing that reducing to pivotal statistics is not always sample-efficient.
conclusion: Although pivotal reduction is elegant, it is not optimal for watermark proportion estimation; full observation provides better sample efficiency.

title: Controlling Isomer Population Using A Dual-Oscillator Infrared Free-Electron Laser
authors: América Y. Torres-Boy, Anoushka Ghosh, Myles B. T. Osenton, Akash C. Behera, Sandy Gewinner, Marco de Pas, Heinz Junkes, Wieland Schöllkopf, Alexander Paarmann, Gert von Helden, And Gerard Meijer

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave events and X-ray pulse profiles, compared to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized.
conclusion: Future observations will further constrain the equation of state, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars

abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and diagnostics.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: It provides an updated understanding of the nuclear physics governing hydrogen burning in main-sequence stars.
conclusion: The paper consolidates recent progress but does not contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Personal narrative and reflection.
result: No technical result; a lecture on the philosophy and practice of physics.
conclusion: Physics is a point of view that shapes how we understand the world.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; real-space methods offer direct access.
method: Reviews three techniques: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use.
result: The paper surveys applications of these techniques to compound semiconductors, highlighting cases where multiple probes provide a complete picture of defects.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques are powerful for characterizing disorder in semiconductors, especially when used in combination.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is important for astrophysics, but the paper does not address the user's research interests in quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches to low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
result: It summarizes the state of the art in nuclear reaction theory for stellar burning.
conclusion: The paper is a comprehensive review of nuclear astrophysics, with no relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties.
result: A self-consistent set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values represent the best current knowledge of fundamental constants, superseding previous sets.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: The paper summarizes the state of the art in optoacoustic microscopy and its applications.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological imaging, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory applied to buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding morphological instabilities in soft materials is important for materials science and biology, but the paper does not address quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and related phenomena in growing soft matter.
conclusion: The paper is a comprehensive review of classical elasticity and buckling, with no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Deterministic Initiation Of Inner-shell X-ray Lasers By Two-color Raman Driving
authors: Carles Serrat
abstract: Inner-shell x-ray lasers are conventionally initiated by amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), so that the temporal onset and longitudinal phase of the emitted field are determined by microscopic noise fluctuations. As a result, the early-time dynamics of the laser pulse are intrinsically stochastic. We analyze a regime in which the initial polarization that triggers inner-shell x-ray lasing is imposed deterministically by a resonant two-color Raman drive. Two coherent x-ray fields at angular frequencies and satisfying induce a core–valence coherence at the lasing frequency through an off-resonant Raman coupling mediated by virtual intermediate states. No electromagnetic field is applied at , and population inversion is generated independently by conventional inner-shell photoionization.
