The Raman-driven coherence therefore acts as an intrinsic microscopic seed for stimulated K emission in the linear small-signal regime, without modifying the underlying gain mechanism. This deterministically seeded operating regime will be referred to as resonant x-ray difference-frequency lasing. Within a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell–Bloch–Langevin propagation model with calibrated spontaneous-emission noise, we derive an explicit analytical criterion separating a noise-dominated ASE regime from a coherence-dominated seeded regime within a finite temporal overlap window. The criterion depends only on the dimensionless Raman drive amplitude, accumulated small-signal gain, gate duration, and calibrated noise strength. Numerical integration of the stochastic propagation equations in dimensionless form confirms the predicted crossover for the same parameter set used in the analytical criterion. These results identify a coherence-dominated operating regime of inner-shell x-ray lasing in which the origin of the amplified field is shifted from spontaneous fluctuations to a driven microscopic coherence, while the gain dynamics remain unchanged. The mechanism requires two-color x-ray fields with a well-defined relative phase within each shot over the overlap window. A microscopic evaluation of the effective Raman coupling using atomic-structure calculations for Ne provides a quantitative mapping from the analytical threshold to pump intensities. Within a bound-manifold estimate, the corresponding seed-dominance threshold lies in the range – , although this mapping can be shifted by continuum contributions and transient plasma-induced broadening and level shifts not included explicitly in the present model.
tldr: This paper proposes a deterministic seeding mechanism for inner-shell x-ray lasers using two-color Raman driving, shifting the initiation from noise-dominated ASE to coherence-dominated lasing.
motivation: Conventional inner-shell x-ray lasers are initiated by stochastic ASE, leading to unpredictable temporal onset and phase. The authors aim to achieve deterministic control over the lasing initiation.
method: The authors develop a microscopic density-matrix model coupled to a linear Maxwell-Bloch-Langevin propagation equation with calibrated spontaneous-emission noise. They derive an analytical criterion separating noise-dominated and coherence-dominated regimes and validate it with numerical simulations.
result: An explicit analytical criterion is derived that depends on Raman drive amplitude, small-signal gain, gate duration, and noise strength. Numerical integration confirms the predicted crossover, identifying a coherence-dominated regime where the amplified field originates from driven coherence rather than spontaneous fluctuations.
conclusion: The mechanism enables deterministic seeding of inner-shell x-ray lasers, requiring two-color x-ray fields with well-defined relative phase. The threshold for seed dominance is estimated for Ne using atomic-structure calculations.

title: The Origin Of Spontaneous Oxidation In A Floating Oil Nanofilm
authors: Patrick J. Herchenbachjeffrey E. Dickahttps://ror.org/02dqehb95department Of Chemistry, Purdue University, West Lafayette, IN 47907bhttps://ror.org/02dqehb95elmore Family School Of Electrical And Computer Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, IN 47907
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 26, June 2026.
SignificanceLiquid|liquid interfaces are central to environmental, biological, and industrial chemistry, where they enable spontaneous reactions that are slow and difficult to observe under bulk conditions. Here, we introduce a floating liquid nanofilm as ...
tldr: This paper studies spontaneous oxidation at liquid-liquid interfaces using a floating oil nanofilm, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand spontaneous reactions at liquid-liquid interfaces, which are important in environmental and industrial chemistry but difficult to observe under bulk conditions.
method: Introduces a floating liquid nanofilm platform to observe and analyze spontaneous oxidation reactions at the interface.
result: The nanofilm enables direct observation of spontaneous oxidation, revealing kinetics and mechanisms not accessible in bulk.
conclusion: The floating nanofilm technique provides a new tool for studying interfacial chemistry, with implications for understanding natural and industrial processes.

title: Detecting Silent Whales Using Seabed Fiber-optic Cables
authors: Robin André Rørstadbotnenmartin Landrøahttps://ror.org/05xg72x27acoustics Group, Department Of Electronic Systems, Norwegian University Of Science And Technology, Trondheim 7034, Norwaybhttps://ror.org/05xg72x27centre For Geophysical Forecasting, Department Of Electronic Systems, Norwegian University Of Science And Technology, Trondheim 7034, Norway
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 26, June 2026.
SignificanceWith present-day acoustic listening technology using seabed fiber-optic cables, it is possible to record and reconstruct the vocalizations of marine mammals. This can be used to track them. However, up to present, it has not been possible to ...
tldr: This paper uses seabed fiber-optic cables to detect and track silent whales by sensing acoustic vibrations.
motivation: Current methods for monitoring marine mammals rely on vocalizations, but many whales are silent or produce sounds outside human hearing range. There is a need for passive detection of silent whales.
method: The authors use distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) on existing seabed fiber-optic cables to measure minute strain changes caused by whale movements and breathing, reconstructing their trajectories.
result: They demonstrate successful detection and tracking of silent whales over several kilometers, showing that fiber-optic cables can serve as a continuous monitoring network.
conclusion: Seabed fiber-optic cables offer a scalable, non-invasive method for monitoring marine mammals, including silent species, with potential applications in ecology and conservation.

title: Unequal Access To Power In Corruption Networks: Evidence From Colombia
authors: Giovanna Rodr\'iguez-Garc\'ia, Mar\'ia Elizabeth Mesa-Pineda, Jos\'e R. Nicol\'as-Carlock
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Corruption is embedded in networks of access, coordination, and protection, yet little is known about how gender shapes actors' positions within them. This article examines whether corruption networks in Colombia's territorial press reproduce gendered patterns of exclusion. Drawing on an access-to-power perspective, we argue that women's lower presence may reflect unequal incorporation into the spaces where exchanges are organized. Empirically, we use Transparencia por Colombia's Radiograf\'ia de Hechos de Corrupci\'on, integrating case- and actor-level information to build co-participation networks. We analyze gender differences in composition, position, recurrence, and institutional access to resources. Results show that these networks are strongly masculinized: men dominate actors and ties, and women appear less often among recurrent actors. However, women are not absent from connected or dense areas, suggesting uneven rather than absolute exclusion. The findings shift attention from whether women are ''less corrupt'' to how unequal access to power structures participation in corruption networks.
tldr: This paper studies gender inequality in corruption networks in Colombia, using network analysis to examine women's access to power.
motivation: To understand how gender shapes participation in corruption networks, moving beyond the question of whether women are 'less corrupt' to how unequal access to power structures involvement.
method: Constructs co-participation networks from Transparencia por Colombia's database of corruption cases, analyzing gender differences in network composition, position, recurrence, and institutional access.
result: Corruption networks are strongly masculinized; men dominate actors and ties, but women are not absent from connected areas, indicating uneven rather than absolute exclusion.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of unequal access to power in shaping gender disparities in corruption networks, shifting focus from individual morality to structural inequality.

title: Scattering, Bound States, And Resonances In The One-dimensional Dirac Equation Via Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanics
authors: Camila C. Soares, Luis B. Castro, Antonio S. de Castro
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified treatment of scattering and discrete spectra for the one-dimensional Dirac equation with scalar and vector interactions. Under the spin-symmetry condition, the coupled first-order Dirac system maps exactly onto an effective Sturm--Liouville (Schr\"o\-din\-ger-like) problem for a single spinor component. This mapping provides a convenient framework for analyzing transmission, reflection, and analytic continuation. As an explicit application, we consider effective interactions of hyperbolic P\"oschl--Teller type and exploit supersymmetric quantum mechanics and shape invariance to obtain a closed-form expression for the transmission probability. The bound-state spectrum is then recovered from the poles of the analytically continued transmission amplitude, reproducing known results and offering a unified description of scattering and bound states. For the barrier configuration, we briefly comment on the resulting pole pattern in the complex momentum plane and its connection with resonance and quasi-normal-mode behavior. Moreover, we use the chiral transformation to relate the spin- and pseudospin-symmetry sectors and translate results between them without repeating the full derivation.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Fractal-Fractional Hiv Dynamics With Mittag-Leffler Kernel: Analysis, Stability, And Numerical Simulations
authors: Samad Noeiaghdam Niaz Ali Shah
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a fractal--fractional HIV model with the Mittag--Leffler kernel is proposed using the Atangana--Baleanu--Caputo operator to capture the memory and hereditary properties of the disease dynamics. The existence and uniqueness of the solutions are investigated using suitable analytical techniques, and the Hyers--Ulam stability analysis is carried out to verify the stability behavior of the proposed system. For the numerical simulations, the Newton polynomial approximation method together with the Atangana--Toufik numerical scheme is employed to obtain approximate solutions for different parameter settings. Furthermore, several visualization techniques, including sensitivity heatmap representation and tornado diagram analysis, are utilized to study the influence of model parameters on the HIV dynamics. The obtained numerical results demonstrate that the proposed fractal--fractional framework provides an effective and reliable approach for analyzing the transient and long-term behavior of HIV transmission dynamics.
tldr: This paper proposes a fractal-fractional HIV model using the Atangana-Baleanu-Caputo operator and analyzes its stability and numerical solutions.
motivation: To capture memory and hereditary properties in HIV transmission dynamics using advanced fractional calculus.
method: The authors use the Atangana-Baleanu-Caputo operator, prove existence and uniqueness of solutions, perform Hyers-Ulam stability analysis, and employ Newton polynomial approximation with the Atangana-Toufik scheme for numerical simulations.
result: Numerical results show the fractal-fractional framework effectively models transient and long-term HIV dynamics, with sensitivity analysis highlighting parameter influences.
conclusion: The proposed model provides a reliable approach for analyzing HIV transmission dynamics, but the work is purely mathematical and epidemiological, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Priori Integral Persistent Excitation In Conservative Polynomial ODEs With Higher-Order Interactions
authors: Alexander Fradkov Aleksandr Semenov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper proposes an approach for verifying integral persistent excitation, which is important in problems of parameter identification and adaptive control in nonlinear dynamical systems. The approach works for conservative polynomial ODEs a priori without knowledge of the parameters. Rigorous proofs of the corresponding theorems are provided. An example of a nonlinear dynamical system with higher-order interactions and the application of the proposed method to it are analyzed. The proof of the main result is formalized in the Lean formal verification language.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for verifying integral persistent excitation in conservative polynomial ODEs with higher-order interactions, with proofs formalized in Lean.
motivation: Integral persistent excitation is important for parameter identification and adaptive control in nonlinear dynamical systems, but verifying it a priori without parameter knowledge is challenging.
method: The approach works for conservative polynomial ODEs and provides rigorous proofs of the corresponding theorems, with the main result formalized in the Lean formal verification language.
result: The method is demonstrated on a nonlinear dynamical system with higher-order interactions, showing its applicability.
conclusion: The paper contributes to control theory and formal verification, but does not relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Operators On Orlicz Sequence Spaces And $\Delta_2$-fundamentality
authors: David E. Edmunds, Jan Krej\v{c}\'i, Zden\v{e}k Mihula, Lubo\v{s} Pick
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical result states that the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator is bounded on an Orlicz space [MATH] if and only if its conjugate Young function [MATH] satisfies the [MATH]-condition. The same condition also characterizes the boundedness on [MATH] of the Hardy averaging operator. We consider a discrete analogue of the problem, extended to a general interpolation framework. We offer several characterizing conditions for the boundedness of discrete maximal and average operators on Orlicz spaces. Although the principal result is as expected, for its proof some new techniques have to be developed. To this end, we introduce a new notion of the so-called [MATH]-fundamental sequence, and give its interesting characterization by a simple condition involving only a limes superior of the ratio of two subsequent terms. We also prove a dual statement concerning operators of Copson type.
tldr: This paper studies boundedness of discrete maximal and average operators on Orlicz sequence spaces, introducing Δ2-fundamental sequences.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize boundedness of discrete analogues of classical operators on Orlicz spaces, extending known results from function spaces to sequence spaces.
method: They develop a new notion of Δ2-fundamental sequences and use interpolation theory to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for boundedness.
result: The boundedness of discrete maximal and averaging operators on Orlicz sequence spaces is characterized by a Δ2-condition on the conjugate Young function, with a dual result for Copson-type operators.
conclusion: The work provides a complete discrete analogue of classical results, with novel proof techniques involving Δ2-fundamental sequences.

title: Worst-Case Maximal Inequalities For Heavy-tailed Random Vectors
authors: Woonyoung Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes finite-sample worst-case maximal inequalities for averages of independent centered heavy-tailed random vectors. The object of interest is the expected top-[MATH] Euclidean norm of the sample average, which includes the expected coordinate-wise maximum as the special case [MATH]. Under coordinatewise variance constraints and tail-envelope constraints, the worst-case value is characterized up to universal constants over the class of distributions satisfying a finite [MATH]:th envelope moment condition. Analogous bounds are obtained for the sub-Weibull envelope class and the marginal sub-Weibull class.
tldr: This paper establishes finite-sample worst-case maximal inequalities for averages of independent heavy-tailed random vectors.
motivation: Heavy-tailed distributions are common in many fields, and understanding the worst-case behavior of sample averages is important for robust statistics.
method: The paper derives bounds under coordinatewise variance and tail-envelope constraints, characterizing the worst-case expected top-k Euclidean norm up to universal constants.
result: The worst-case value is characterized for distributions satisfying a finite p-th envelope moment condition, with analogous bounds for sub-Weibull classes.
conclusion: The results provide tight maximal inequalities for heavy-tailed vectors, but the paper is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On One Relaxation Of The Bounded-length-distortion Condition In The Context Of Metric Measure Spaces
authors: Roman D. Oleinik
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reformulate the bounded-length-distortion condition for maps between metric spaces in a certain relaxed form that requires the presence of a reference measure on the source space, which makes the new approach more natural from the perspective of maps from metric measure spaces to metric spaces. In terms of the introduced notion, we establish some mapping results in an entirely singular setting of the following general structure: a metric measure space of finite Hausdorff dimension admits a map with the relaxed bounded-length-distortion condition into a finite-dimensional normed space.
tldr: The paper relaxes the bounded-length-distortion condition for maps between metric spaces using a reference measure, establishing mapping results for metric measure spaces into finite-dimensional normed spaces.
motivation: To generalize the bounded-length-distortion condition to a setting that incorporates a reference measure, making it more natural for maps from metric measure spaces.
method: The author introduces a relaxed version of the bounded-length-distortion condition that requires a reference measure on the source space, and then proves mapping theorems for metric measure spaces of finite Hausdorff dimension into finite-dimensional normed spaces.
result: The paper establishes that a metric measure space of finite Hausdorff dimension admits a map with the relaxed bounded-length-distortion condition into a finite-dimensional normed space.
conclusion: The relaxed condition allows for mapping results in a singular setting, extending the theory of metric embeddings to metric measure spaces.

title: Killing The Case For Randomization In Dynamic Assortment Optimization
authors: Huseyin Topaloglu Mikhail Fadin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the traditional approaches for constructing approximate policies for dynamic assortment optimization problems is to use sampling-based inventory-agnostic policies. Such policies are called sampling-based, as they sample an assortment of products from a fixed distribution at each time period to offer to a customer of each type. Such policies are called inventory-agnostic, as the sampled assortments may include products without remaining inventories, so if a customer chooses a product without remaining inventories, then she leaves without a purchase. Inventory-agnostic nature of a policy is not a concern, because it is known that if the policy samples an assortment that includes products without remaining inventories, then dropping the products without remaining inventories does not degrade the performance. However, sampling-based nature of a policy is a concern, because sampling brings another source of uncertainty in the performance. In this paper, we give an algorithm to de-randomize any sampling-based inventory-agnostic policy, so the de-randomized policy offers a deterministic sequence of assortments within the support of the original policy without degrading the performance. Furthermore, we give a variation of our de-randomization algorithm that searches for a deterministic sequence of assortments beyond the support of the original policy. We show that we can implement the latter variation efficiently as long as we can solve the static assortment optimization problem under the choice model governing the choice process of the customers. As our crowning technical contribution, we study locally-optimal deterministic policies, where changing any single one of the assortments in the policy does not improve the total expected revenue. We show that any locally-optimal policy has a performance guarantee of 1/2 - epsilon when compared with the best sampling-based policy.
tldr: This paper addresses dynamic assortment optimization in operations research, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to de-randomize sampling-based inventory-agnostic policies for dynamic assortment optimization to reduce uncertainty.
method: The authors propose an algorithm to convert any sampling-based policy into a deterministic sequence of assortments without performance loss, and a variation that searches beyond the original support.
result: They show that any locally-optimal deterministic policy achieves a performance guarantee of 1/2 - epsilon compared to the best sampling-based policy.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical guarantees for deterministic policies in dynamic assortment optimization, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ergodicity And High-Frequency Inference For Hybrid Switching L\'{e}vy-Driven Stochastic Differential Equations
authors: Yuzhong Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid switching L\'evy-driven stochastic differential equations with pure-jump noise and state-dependent switching rates are studied under high-frequency observation. A three-stage inference procedure is proposed for the drift, scale, and switching-rate parameters, combining a staged Gaussian quasi-likelihood with an intensity-type contrast. Checkable sufficient conditions for weighted exponential ergodicity are established for the hybrid process; the proof does not rely on Brownian smoothing, but uses a fixed skeleton-chain argument combining small-jump accessibility and regime connectivity. Under ergodicity and the high-frequency sampling scheme, consistency, joint asymptotic normality, and a polynomial-type large deviation inequality are proved for the full estimator. The joint limit exhibits a transparent covariance structure: the drift and scale blocks are coupled through the third moment of the driving L\'evy noise, whereas the switching-rate block is asymptotically uncorrelated with the continuous-coefficient blocks. Numerical experiments for models driven by normal inverse Gaussian noise illustrate the finite-sample behavior of the proposed estimators.
tldr: This paper studies statistical inference for hybrid switching Lévy-driven stochastic differential equations under high-frequency observation.
motivation: The paper aims to develop estimation methods for a class of stochastic processes with jumps and state-dependent switching, which are relevant in finance and other fields.
method: A three-stage inference procedure combining Gaussian quasi-likelihood and intensity-type contrast is proposed, and ergodicity is established using a fixed skeleton-chain argument.
result: Consistency, asymptotic normality, and large deviation inequalities are proved for the estimators, with a transparent covariance structure.
conclusion: The proposed method works well in numerical experiments, but the paper has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relaxed Lagrange Multiplier (rlm) Schemes For Phase Field Models Preserving The Relaxed Original Energy Dissipation Law
authors: Jia Zhao Xiaobo Jing
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-field models are typically derived from variational principles for a free-energy functional and are widely used to simulate complex multiphase phenomena in science and engineering. A central goal in designing numerical schemes for these models is to preserve the underlying energy-dissipation law. In this paper, we propose a class of relaxed Lagrange multiplier (RLM) schemes for phase field models. In contrast to popular scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) and invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) methods, which dissipate a modified energy involving auxiliary variables, the RLM schemes dissipate a relaxed version of the original energy and closely track the original energy dissipation rate. Compared with the classical Lagrange multiplier (LM) approach, the RLM schemes ensure that the resulting discrete system is uniquely solvable over a broad range of time steps. The key idea is to augment the LM formulation with a relaxation term, yielding a scalar quadratic equation for the multiplier with an explicit closed-form solution. The resulting schemes are linear and efficient because each time step requires solving only two linear systems with constant coefficients, at a cost comparable to that of SAV schemes. We construct both first-order and second-order variants and prove their energy stability. Numerical experiments verify the expected convergence rates and demonstrate that the RLM schemes accurately capture interface dynamics.
tldr: This paper proposes relaxed Lagrange multiplier schemes for phase field models to preserve energy dissipation laws.
motivation: Phase field models are widely used in multiphase simulations, and preserving the original energy dissipation law is crucial for numerical accuracy.
method: The authors introduce a relaxation term to the Lagrange multiplier formulation, resulting in a scalar quadratic equation with an explicit solution, leading to linear schemes requiring only two constant-coefficient linear systems per time step.
result: First- and second-order RLM schemes are constructed, proven energy stable, and validated through numerical experiments showing expected convergence and accurate interface dynamics.
conclusion: RLM schemes offer an efficient and accurate alternative to SAV and IEQ methods for phase field models, preserving a relaxed original energy dissipation law.

title: Regularized Model Predictive Control Via Contractivity And Implicit Lur'e Analysis
authors: Ryotaro Shima, Anand Gokhale, Alexander Davydov, Francesco Bullo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a contraction-based stability analysis for regularized model predictive control (MPC), whose feedback law is defined implicitly by a finite-horizon optimal control problem with an additional regularizing cost. The proposed approach interprets regularized MPC as an implicit Lur'e system, in which the regularizing cost perturbs the optimality conditions. We develop a multiplier-based contraction framework for implicit Lur'e systems and derive linear matrix inequality conditions for regularized MPC with three broad classes of regularizers: convex smooth stage costs, convex closed proper stage costs, and differentiable regularizers with Lipschitz gradients. Numerical studies on input and state soft penalties, hard input constraints, and sparsity-promoting penalties illustrate that regularization shapes closed-loop performance while retaining formal contraction-based stability guarantees.
tldr: This paper develops a contraction-based stability analysis for regularized model predictive control using an implicit Lur'e system framework.
motivation: Regularized MPC is widely used but lacks formal stability guarantees; the paper aims to provide a systematic method to certify contraction and stability for a broad class of regularizers.
method: The approach interprets regularized MPC as an implicit Lur'e system and derives linear matrix inequality conditions for contraction using multiplier theory.
result: The framework yields stability guarantees for convex smooth, convex closed proper, and differentiable regularizers with Lipschitz gradients, demonstrated on input/state soft penalties, hard constraints, and sparsity-promoting penalties.
conclusion: Regularization can shape closed-loop performance while retaining formal contraction-based stability, enabling safe and efficient MPC design.

title: Exponential Low-Regularity Parareal Algorithms For Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equations
authors: Zhi Zhou Qingle Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The parareal algorithm is one of the most widely studied parallel-in-time methods for the numerical approximation of time-dependent problems. For non-diffusive equations, however, standard parareal methods may converge slowly or even become unstable due to the absence of damping, while nonlinear interactions can transfer and amplify phase errors across Fourier modes. In this work, we consider the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLS) as a representative non-diffusive model and analyze parareal algorithms with an exact fine propagator, with particular emphasis on the design of suitable coarse propagators. We establish a general convergence framework, valid for solutions with limited regularity, under stability and local truncation error assumptions on the coarse propagator. These assumptions are verified for selected exponential low-regularity integrators designed for one-dimensional quadratic and cubic NLS equations, which achieve optimal approximation orders without derivative loss. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of parareal algorithms for NLS equations that are provably linearly convergent, with a contraction factor proportional to the coarse time-step size even for solutions of limited regularity. Numerical experiments on quadratic, cubic, and quintic NLS equations demonstrate rapid convergence and improved performance over parareal variants using classical coarse propagators, including Lie and Strang splitting methods and first- and third-order exponential Runge--Kutta integrators.
tldr: This paper develops exponential low-regularity parareal algorithms for nonlinear Schrödinger equations, focusing on numerical analysis and parallel-in-time integration.
motivation: Standard parareal methods converge slowly or become unstable for non-diffusive equations like NLS due to lack of damping and nonlinear phase errors.
method: The authors design coarse propagators using exponential low-regularity integrators and prove linear convergence under stability and local truncation error assumptions.
result: First provably linearly convergent parareal algorithms for NLS with contraction factor proportional to coarse time-step size, even for low-regularity solutions.
conclusion: The proposed algorithms show rapid convergence and outperform classical coarse propagators in numerical experiments.

title: Resonance Structure Of A Periodically Forced Delay Differential Equation Model For The El Ni\~no--Southern Oscillation
authors: Samuel Bolduc-St-Aubin, Priya Subramanian, Bernd Krauskopf
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study resonance phenomena in the periodically forced Suarez--Schopf delay differential equation, which is a conceptual climate model for the El Ni\~no--Southern Oscillation (ENSO). The system serves as a prototypical forced delayed-action oscillator whose self-sustained oscillations, when subjected to periodic forcing, give rise to attracting invariant tori. We provide a comprehensive bifurcation analysis of both the unforced and the forced model; for the latter, we propose a method to compute the rotation number of normally hyperbolic attracting invariant tori. With it we show that resonance tongues in parameter space are organized by critical points of the graph of the rotation number, both along torus bifurcation curves and within the region of invariant tori. We also show that the resonance structure repeats for large delays, which constitutes a reappearance mechanism not previously reported in the literature. Furthermore, depending on the feedback strength, we find bistability between period-one orbits and invariant tori. This regime involves non-classical bifurcation sequences, including `saddle-node' and `gluing' bifurcations of tori.
tldr: This paper studies resonance phenomena in a delay differential equation model for ENSO, a climate oscillation.
motivation: Understanding resonance structures in forced delay differential equations is important for climate modeling.
method: Bifurcation analysis of the Suarez-Schopf model, computing rotation numbers of invariant tori.
result: Resonance tongues are organized by critical points of the rotation number; bistability between period-one orbits and tori is found.
conclusion: The resonance structure repeats for large delays, revealing a reappearance mechanism.

title: When Self-Protection Backfires: Adaptive Contact Behavior Expands The Endemic Basin In An Addiction Model With Nonlinear Relapse
authors: Fabio Sanchez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the Susceptible--Addicted--Reformed (SAR) model of , which exhibits a forward--backward bifurcation driven by nonlinear relapse, by embedding an epi-economic behavioral layer in the spirit of . At-risk individuals choose contact levels by solving a finite-horizon dynamic program that balances the utility of social activity against the expected cost of addiction. We prove that the basic reproduction number \( R_0 \) and the local stability of the addiction-free equilibrium remain unchanged by the behavioral layer. However, the endemic structure is fundamentally altered: the behavioral response collapses exactly to a scalar mixing factor \( M \), and the bifurcation curve factorizes as \( R_0(a) = R_{\rm cl}(a)/M(a) \). This yields an exact comparison principle: the saddle-node fold shifts to lower \( R_0 \) (enlarging the endemic basin) if and only if \( M \ge 1 \) along the branch. For rational self-protective behavior under conditional proportional mixing, we prove \( M \ge 1 \), so the basin enlarges; the opposite holds under frequency-dependent mixing. Numerical continuation shows that, at baseline parameters, the fold moves left by \( \Delta R_0 \approx -0.035 \) and the critical initial addiction level drops by 2--6 percentage points. Gillespie simulations confirm that the enlarged basin increases the stochastic probability of addiction establishment by up to threefold near threshold. This counterintuitive result that rational self-protection can make addiction easier to establish has direct implications for prevention policy.
tldr: This paper studies an epidemiological model of addiction with adaptive contact behavior, showing that rational self-protection can paradoxically enlarge the endemic basin.
motivation: To understand how individual behavioral responses to addiction risk affect the population-level dynamics of addiction, particularly the stability of endemic states.
method: Extends the Susceptible-Addicted-Reformed (SAR) model with an epi-economic behavioral layer where at-risk individuals optimize contact levels via dynamic programming; uses bifurcation analysis and Gillespie simulations.
result: The behavioral response collapses to a scalar mixing factor M; under conditional proportional mixing, M ≥ 1 shifts the saddle-node fold to lower R0, enlarging the endemic basin and increasing stochastic addiction probability up to threefold.
conclusion: Rational self-protection can backfire by making addiction easier to establish, with implications for prevention policy.

title: An Inner-Outer Iteration Algorithm With Optimal Parameters For Stochastic Lyapunov Matrix Equation
authors: Donghuan He, Xiaowen Su, Feng Wang, Xuesong Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes an inner--outer (IO) iterative algorithm with optimal parameters for solving stochastic Lyapunov matrix equation associated with discrete-time stochastic linear system. First, under the assumption that the underlying stochastic linear system is asymptotically mean-square stable, the monotonicity and boundedness of the iterative sequence generated by the proposed algorithm are analyzed. On this basis, a sufficient convergence result is established for the zero initial condition. Second, by deriving the spectral radius of the corresponding iteration matrix, several necessary and sufficient convergence conditions are obtained for arbitrary initial conditions. In addition, the optimal parameter-selection strategies are developed to improve the convergence performance of the algorithm. Finally, numerical examples are presented to verify the theoretical results and demonstrate the advantages of the proposed algorithm over several existing iterative methods.
tldr: This paper proposes an iterative algorithm with optimal parameters for solving the stochastic Lyapunov matrix equation, which is a numerical linear algebra problem.
motivation: Efficiently solving stochastic Lyapunov matrix equations is important for analyzing discrete-time stochastic linear systems, but existing methods may have slow convergence.
method: The authors develop an inner-outer iteration algorithm and derive optimal parameter selection strategies to improve convergence, analyzing monotonicity and spectral radius of the iteration matrix.
result: The algorithm achieves faster convergence compared to existing iterative methods, as demonstrated by numerical examples.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm with optimal parameters is an effective numerical method for solving stochastic Lyapunov matrix equations.

title: Periodic Orbits With Prescribed Negative Energy For Relativistic Keplerian Problems
authors: Alberto Boscaggin, Guglielmo Feltrin, Duccio Papini
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a variational approach, we study the existence of periodic solutions with prescribed energy for the relativistic equation }{t}\left({|^{2}/c^{2}}}\right) = -\alpha {|x|^{3}} + \nabla W(x), \qquad x\in^{N}\setminus\{0\}, where [MATH] is a lower-order perturbation of the Kepler potential. The main difficulty stems from the fact that the Kepler singularity is critical for the associated Maupertuis functional, lying exactly at the boundary between the weak force and strong force regimes. To overcome the resulting lack of compactness, we use a penalization procedure and develop a suitable min-max scheme combined with a blow-up analysis of near-collision critical sequences. As a consequence, we establish the existence of periodic solutions on prescribed negative energy levels, obtaining non-perturbative results in every dimension [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies periodic orbits in relativistic Keplerian problems using variational methods, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To prove existence of periodic solutions with prescribed negative energy for a relativistic Kepler equation with a perturbed Kepler potential.
method: Uses a variational approach with a penalization procedure and min-max scheme combined with blow-up analysis of near-collision critical sequences.
result: Establishes existence of periodic solutions on prescribed negative energy levels for all dimensions.
conclusion: The work is purely mathematical and classical, unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Exponential Sigmoid Equation For Modelling Cell Growth In A Confined Space, Log-Normal Distribution For Modelling Cell Area Distribution Of Dense Colonies And Other Methods
authors: Brad Turner Kavinda Jayawardana
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the growth patterns of 166 CHO monoclones observed over a 15 day period, we show that the standard population growth in a confined space equation, i.e. the sigmoid/logistic function, is alone does not capture the complex behaviour of the cell growth in a confined space. Thus, combining the sigmoid function and the exponential of the sigmoid function, we present a more accurate model for modelling cell growth in a confined space. We also present a working algorithm to obtain population growth variables (growth capacity, growth time and growth rate), model the growth patterns of the CHO monoclones, and we include subset of the dataset, along with a sample python script for the reader to replicate the results. Furthermore, we derive a model for cell confluence growth in a confined space, numerically model the confluence and present the reader with a working algorithm. With Kolmogorov-Smirnov analysis conducted on the area of the CHO monoclones, we show that the cell area of the incipient population is normally distributed, the sparse cell population is gamma distributed and the dense colony population is log-normally distributed. Thus, we further derive models for the mean, the standard deviation, the coefficient of variation and the inverse coefficient of variation for the log cell area growth in a confined space, numerically model them and present the reader with working algorithms. Finally, based on the growth patterns of another 48 CHO monoclones observed over a 16 day period, and their titer and viability measurements, we find the correlation coefficients with our calculated growth variables, and titer and viability measurements, and show that our derived growth variables can be used to predict the productivity and the health of a cell. Thus, we conclude our study by demonstrating that the productivity and the health of a cell (also the overall population) are interdependent.
tldr: This paper models cell growth in confined spaces using an exponential sigmoid equation and analyzes cell area distributions, with applications to predicting cell productivity and health.
motivation: Standard sigmoid/logistic functions fail to capture complex cell growth behavior in confined spaces, motivating a more accurate model.
method: Combines sigmoid and exponential sigmoid functions to model growth; uses Kolmogorov-Smirnov analysis to determine cell area distributions (normal, gamma, log-normal) at different stages.
result: Derived growth variables correlate with titer and viability measurements, enabling prediction of cell productivity and health.
conclusion: Cell productivity and health are interdependent, and the proposed growth variables can serve as predictors.

title: A Nonstandard Finite Difference Scheme For A Nonlinear Parabolic Equation With p-Laplacian-Type Diffusion
authors: Achraf Zinihi, Matthias Ehrhardt, Moulay Rchid Sidi Ammi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) scheme for nonlinear parabolic equations involving a p-Laplacian-type diffusion operator in one- and two-dimensional spatial domains. Following Mickens' design principles, the proposed discretization employs a nonlinear denominator function phi(.) together with a nonlocal approximation of the nonlinear diffusion term Delta_p, yielding a structure-preserving discrete model. The scheme is designed to retain key qualitative properties of the continuous problem, including positivity, boundedness, and stability, which may be lost by standard finite difference methods (FDMs). We establish the well-posedness of the continuous model, derive the NSFD scheme, and investigate its consistency, convergence, and local truncation error. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results and demonstrate that, unlike the standard explicit FDM, the proposed NSFD scheme avoids spurious oscillations and nonphysical negative solutions even for relatively large time-step sizes.
tldr: This paper proposes a nonstandard finite difference scheme for nonlinear parabolic equations with p-Laplacian-type diffusion, focusing on numerical stability and structure preservation.
motivation: Standard finite difference methods often produce spurious oscillations or negative solutions for such equations; a structure-preserving scheme is needed.
method: The authors design an NSFD scheme using a nonlinear denominator function and nonlocal approximation of the p-Laplacian, following Mickens' principles.
result: The scheme is proven to preserve positivity, boundedness, and stability, and numerical experiments confirm it avoids nonphysical solutions even with large time steps.
conclusion: The proposed NSFD scheme is a reliable numerical method for p-Laplacian-type diffusion problems, outperforming standard explicit FDMs.

title: A Minimax Approach To Relative Periodic Orbits In Symmetric Three-Degree-of-Freedom Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Mitsuru Shibayama Shu Sakaguchi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study three-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian systems that are invariant under rotations about the [MATH]-axis and under reflection across the [MATH]-plane. Fixing the angular momentum, such systems reduce to Hamiltonian systems with two degrees of freedom. We focus on the range of energy values for which the corresponding Hill regions are compact. First, under suitable assumptions on the topology of these compact Hill regions, we prove the existence of periodic solutions on each prescribed energy surface of the reduced system by means of a variational minimax method. These periodic solutions are obtained as saddle points of the Maupertuis functional. The resulting solutions are either nontrivial spatial periodic solutions or trivial planar brake solutions in the reduced system. Next, by computing the Morse index, we provide a sufficient condition ensuring that the periodic solutions obtained are nontrivial. Finally, we apply our results to the isosceles three-body problem and to the spatial anisotropic Kepler problem. In both cases, we verify the sufficient condition for nontriviality and thereby establish the existence of nontrivial periodic solutions.
tldr: This paper studies periodic orbits in symmetric three-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian systems using a variational minimax method, applied to the isosceles three-body problem and spatial anisotropic Kepler problem.
motivation: The authors aim to prove existence of nontrivial periodic solutions in reduced Hamiltonian systems with two degrees of freedom, under compact Hill regions.
method: A variational minimax approach is used, treating periodic solutions as saddle points of the Maupertuis functional, with Morse index computation to ensure nontriviality.
result: Existence of nontrivial spatial periodic solutions is established under topological assumptions, and the sufficient condition is verified for the isosceles three-body problem and spatial anisotropic Kepler problem.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous existence proof for periodic orbits in classical Hamiltonian systems, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Failure Of Convex-Hull Bounds Under Log-Convex Tails
authors: Hanchao Wang Xuanang Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fix [MATH], and let [MATH] be independent symmetric Weibull[MATH] random variables, that is, \[ (|X_i|>t)=e^{-t^r},\qquad t\ge 0. \] We prove that there is no constant [MATH], depending only on [MATH], with the following universal property: for every finite set [MATH] there exists a sequence [MATH] such that \[ T-T\subset conv\{y_k:k\ge 1\}, \qquad \|X_{y_k}\|_{L_{\log(k+2)}}\le C_r\,\bx(T) \quad (k\ge 1), \] where [MATH] and [MATH]. This gives a negative answer to a question of Lata{\l}a concerning the validity of convex-hull bounds for canonical Weibull processes. In fact, the failure persists even when the auxiliary vectors appearing in the convex hull are allowed to be arbitrary.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture about convex-hull bounds for Weibull processes, showing that no universal constant exists for log-convex tails.
motivation: The authors aim to answer a question by Latała regarding the validity of convex-hull bounds for canonical Weibull processes with log-convex tails.
method: They construct a counterexample using independent symmetric Weibull random variables and analyze the behavior of the L_{log(k+2)} norms.
result: They prove that there is no constant C_r such that for every finite set T there exists a sequence y_k satisfying the convex-hull property, thus giving a negative answer to Latała's question.
conclusion: The failure of convex-hull bounds under log-convex tails is established, and the result holds even when auxiliary vectors are arbitrary.

title: An Semidefinite Programming-based $\varepsilon$-constraint Method For The Bi-objective Single-row Facility Layout Problem
authors: Christof Brandstetter, Elisabeth Gaar, Markus Sinnl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we introduce a multi-objective version of the well-known single-row facility layout problem (SRFLP). In the SRFLP, a set of one-dimensional facilities should be placed along a single line such that the weighted sum of the center-to-center distances of each pair of facilities is minimized. In our multi-objective extension, there are multiple such weighted-sum objectives which we consider under the concept of Pareto optimality. We develop a solution algorithm based on the [MATH]-constraint method to solve the bi-objective SRFLP. Many existing works on the [MATH]-constraint method use integer linear programming (ILP) solvers in a black-box fashion for solving the problems at the individual iterations of the method. In contrast to that, we use our own branch-and-bound procedure based on semidefinite programming (SDP), as SDP relaxations are known to be more effective for solving the SRFLP than linear programming relaxations of ILPs. This allows us to propose several enhancements procedures for our [MATH]-constraint approach, such as non-binary branching and reusing of nodes within the branch-and-bound trees, which are usually not possible when using black-box solvers. We present a computational study to demonstrate the effectiveness of our solution approach and its enhancements.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-objective extension of the single-row facility layout problem and solves it using an SDP-based ε-constraint method.
motivation: The single-row facility layout problem is a classic optimization problem, and its multi-objective version has practical relevance in facility planning.
method: The authors develop a branch-and-bound procedure based on semidefinite programming relaxations, incorporating enhancements like non-binary branching and node reuse.
result: Computational experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution approach and its enhancements.
conclusion: The SDP-based ε-constraint method is a viable approach for solving bi-objective single-row facility layout problems.

title: Hermite Semi-Lagrangian Schemes On Triangular Meshes For Advection Equations
authors: Ali Elarif (IRMA, MACARON), Michel Mehrenberger (I2M, AMU), Laurent Navoret
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-order Hermite semi-Lagrangian schemes on unstructured triangular grids are proposed for advection equations, based on Bell and Argyris finite elements. Nodal semi-Lagrangian schemes transport point values together with gradients and Hessians, while projection semi-Lagrangian schemes are basically semi-Lagrangian Discontinuous Galerkin schemes (SLDG) with straight remaining backward triangles and shared degrees of freedoms. Stability and convergence studies of the different schemes are carried out numerically.
tldr: This paper develops high-order Hermite semi-Lagrangian schemes on unstructured triangular meshes for solving advection equations.
motivation: To improve accuracy and stability of numerical solutions for advection equations on complex geometries.
method: Uses Bell and Argyris finite elements to transport point values along with gradients and Hessians, and compares nodal and projection semi-Lagrangian approaches.
result: Stability and convergence studies are carried out numerically, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed schemes.
conclusion: The Hermite semi-Lagrangian schemes on triangular meshes provide a viable high-order method for advection problems.

title: Iterative Graph Lifting For Automatic Design Of Path-complete Stability Certificates
authors: Rapha\"el M. Jungers L\'ea Ninite
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stability of switched linear systems under arbitrary switching is a fundamental problem in control theory, closely related to the joint spectral radius (JSR), which characterizes the worst-case growth rate of system trajectories. In this paper, we contribute to the path-complete approach for approximating the JSR. This framework constructs algebraic stability certificates using labeled directed graphs, known as path-complete graphs. These certificates can be computed via an associated optimization problem. We propose an iterative algorithm that refines path-complete graphs in an efficient and parsimonious manner. The algorithm relies on a graph-theoretic analysis of the optimality conditions of the underlying optimization problem. In particular, we derive a sufficient condition under which the exact JSR is attained by a given path-complete graph. When this condition is not satisfied, we identify bottleneck nodes by analyzing the graph induced by the active constraints. We then use this information to refine the path-complete graph via local graph lifting (node splitting), and repeat the procedure. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on all challenging instances tested.
tldr: This paper proposes an iterative graph lifting algorithm for designing path-complete stability certificates for switched linear systems, focusing on the joint spectral radius approximation.
motivation: Stability analysis of switched linear systems is a fundamental control theory problem, and the path-complete approach provides algebraic certificates but often requires manual design.
method: The authors derive optimality conditions for path-complete graphs and identify bottleneck nodes via active constraints, then refine the graph through local node splitting (graph lifting) iteratively.
result: Numerical experiments show the algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods on challenging instances, achieving exact JSR in many cases.
conclusion: The iterative graph lifting method automates the design of path-complete certificates, improving scalability and accuracy for JSR approximation.

title: Approximate Full-conformal Multi-task Regression With Reproducing Kernels
authors: Davidson Lova Razafindrakoto (SAMM), Alain Celisse (SAMM), J\'er\^ome Lacaille
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-task regression aims at jointly solving multiple regression problems, called tasks. Compared to solving each task separately, better performances can be achieved as long as the tasks are sufficiently related. Full-conformal prediction is a framework that formulates a data-dependent prediction-region containing the unknown output-vector at any prescribed confidence level. However, explicit computation of this prediction-region is intractable in general since it requires training infinitely many predictors. The present work focuses on multi-task regression in a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) of vector-valued functions. This computational issue is addressed by designing an approximating predictionregion containing the full-conformal one. This construction is carried out in two scenarios: piq when the inter-task covariance-matrix is known, and piiq when this matrix is estimated. In terms of volume, the tightness of this approximation is assessed theoretically by means of an upper-bound in the first scenario. It is also empirically proved to improve upon the split-conformal prediction on synthetic data in both scenarios.
tldr: This paper proposes an approximate full-conformal prediction region for multi-task regression in RKHS, but is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Exact full-conformal prediction for multi-task regression is computationally intractable; the authors aim to provide a tractable approximation.
method: They design an approximating prediction region that contains the full-conformal one, considering both known and estimated inter-task covariance matrices, and provide theoretical upper bounds on the volume tightness.
result: The approximation is theoretically assessed via an upper bound on volume tightness when covariance is known, and empirically shown to outperform split-conformal prediction on synthetic data.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a computationally feasible alternative to full-conformal prediction for multi-task regression, with theoretical guarantees and empirical validation.

title: Penalty-Free Natural Deep Ritz Method Based On De Rham Complex For High-Dimensional Dirichlet Boundary Value Problems
authors: Jiarong Chen, Xia Ji, Haijun Yu, Shuo Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep neural networks show great promise for high-dimensional PDEs, yet enforcing essential boundary conditions remains challenging, especially as penalty parameters require problem-specific retuning with increasing dimensionality. In this work, we extend the Natural Deep Ritz Method (NatDRM) [H. Yu and S. Zhang, J. Comput. Phys., 537 (2025)] to a unified framework for all dimensions [MATH] based on the de Rham complex and its penalty-free boundary decomposition: curl-type operators act on scalar potentials in 2D, vector potentials in 3D, and antisymmetric second-order tensor potentials in [MATH], respectively. This method converts Dirichlet constraints into three coupled natural (Neumann-type) subproblems with corresponding Ritz-type losses, eliminating the need for a boundary penalty parameter [MATH]. We derive dimension-unified discrete losses, lightweight boundary-based gauge-fixing regularizations to resolve curl-kernel non-uniqueness, and a joint training procedure; extensions to variable-coefficient elliptic and semilinear Poisson problems are formulated at the first subproblem level. Numerical experiments on smooth benchmarks up to 6D show that NatDRM, without any penalty tuning, matches or exceeds the accuracy of optimally tuned DRM and PINN in most cases. It converges stably in 6D where penalized DRM fails for most penalty values, and exhibits synchronous decay of interior and boundary errors, resolving the inherent imbalance of penalty-based methods.
tldr: This paper proposes a penalty-free natural deep Ritz method for high-dimensional Dirichlet boundary value problems using de Rham complex.
motivation: Enforcing essential boundary conditions in deep neural network-based PDE solvers is challenging, especially with penalty parameters that require problem-specific retuning in high dimensions.
method: The method extends the Natural Deep Ritz Method to a unified framework for all dimensions using de Rham complex and penalty-free boundary decomposition, converting Dirichlet constraints into coupled natural subproblems with Ritz-type losses.
result: Numerical experiments up to 6D show that the method matches or exceeds the accuracy of optimally tuned DRM and PINN, converges stably where penalized DRM fails, and resolves the imbalance of penalty-based methods.
conclusion: The proposed method eliminates the need for penalty parameter tuning and provides stable and accurate solutions for high-dimensional Dirichlet problems.

title: Goal-oriented Space-time Adaptivity For The Navier--Stokes Equations Based On The Dual Weighted Residual Method
authors: Marius Paul Bruchh\"auser, Nils Margenberg, Markus Bause
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a goal-oriented a posteriori error estimator based on the Dual Weighted Residual (DWR) method together with space-time mesh adaptivity for the Navier--Stokes equations. The resulting nonlinear algebraic systems on the space-time slabs are solved by Newton's method with GMRES, preconditioned by a slab-wise geometric multigrid method. This combination yields reliable control of target quantities on computationally feasible space-time meshes together with a robust and efficient solution of the algebraic systems. The implementation is based on a MPI-parallel programming model in the deal.II library. Further ingredients are a discontinuous Galerkin discretization in time and inf-sup stable finite element pairs with discontinuous pressure on tensor-product meshes. The performance of the approach is investigated in benchmark computations with regard to accuracy, efficiency, and stability.
tldr: This paper presents a goal-oriented space-time adaptive method for Navier-Stokes equations using the Dual Weighted Residual method.
motivation: To achieve reliable control of target quantities in fluid dynamics simulations with computationally feasible meshes.
method: Combines DWR-based a posteriori error estimation with space-time mesh adaptivity, solved by Newton-GMRES with geometric multigrid preconditioning.
result: Demonstrates accuracy, efficiency, and stability in benchmark computations.
conclusion: The proposed method provides effective goal-oriented adaptivity for Navier-Stokes equations.

title: Actions Of Lattices In $S$-arithmetic Groups On Manifolds
authors: Segev Gonen Cohen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that an action by [MATH] diffeomorphisms of a lattice in a simple [MATH]-adic group on a compact manifold is finite, provided the dimension is less than the rank. We extend this statement to lattices in totally disconnected [MATH]-arithmetic groups, where the critical dimension is the maximal rank of the simple factors. This uses the machinery developed by Brown, Fisher, and Hurtado.
tldr: This paper proves finiteness results for actions of lattices in S-arithmetic groups on compact manifolds of low dimension.
motivation: Understanding when group actions on manifolds must be finite is a fundamental problem in geometric group theory and dynamics.
method: The proof uses machinery developed by Brown, Fisher, and Hurtado, extending previous results to totally disconnected S-arithmetic groups.
result: Actions by diffeomorphisms of a lattice in a simple p-adic group on a compact manifold are finite if the dimension is less than the rank; a similar result holds for lattices in totally disconnected S-arithmetic groups with critical dimension given by the maximal rank of simple factors.
conclusion: The work establishes new constraints on low-dimensional actions of certain arithmetic groups, contributing to the theory of group actions on manifolds.

title: A Linear, Decoupled And Positivity-preserving Time-staggered Block-centered Finite Difference Method For The Multi-species Keller-Segel Chemotaxis System
authors: Ao Zhang, Bingyin Zhang, Hongfei Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a linearly implicit, second-order block-centered finite difference (BCFD) prediction-then-projection scheme for the multi-species Keller-Segel chemotaxis system on non-uniform spatio-temporal grids. The proposed scheme integrates a standard Crank-Nicolson time-marching algorithm with an [MATH] projection step to enforce positivity and mass conservation. The use of variable time stepsize and time-staggered discretization fully decouples the solutions of the multi-species cell density variables and the chemoattractant concentration variable while facilitating linearization, thereby greatly enhancing computational efficiency. Notably, the variable time-stepping algorithm and non-uniform grid BCFD discretization jointly enable adaptive resolution and local refinement near blow-up, thereby improving efficiency and accuracy without compromising the desired physical property-preserving in the simulation. Furthermore, using the mathematical induction method and the energy analysis approach, the unique solvability of the proposed scheme is rigorously proved, and we show that cell densities achieve second-order convergence in both time and space in the discrete [MATH] norm, while the chemoattractant concentration achieves second-order convergence in the discrete [MATH] norm. Representative numerical experiments are presented to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the reliability of the proposed scheme in simulating the blow-up phenomenon.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for solving the multi-species Keller-Segel chemotaxis system, which is a classical PDE model in biology.
motivation: Efficient and accurate simulation of chemotaxis systems is important for understanding biological pattern formation, but existing methods may suffer from high computational cost or lack of positivity preservation.
method: A linearly implicit, second-order block-centered finite difference scheme with a projection step is developed, using variable time steps and non-uniform grids to decouple variables and ensure positivity and mass conservation.
result: The scheme is proven to be uniquely solvable and achieves second-order convergence in both time and space for cell densities and chemoattractant concentration, validated by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed method is reliable for simulating blow-up phenomena in chemotaxis systems, offering improved efficiency and accuracy.

title: Proxy-surface-based Fast Direct Solver For TE-mode Scattering Problems On Distributed Memory Systems
authors: Rio Yokota Yasuhiro Matsumoto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes an MPI/OpenMP hybrid parallelized fast direct solver for the scattering problem of transverse electric (TE)-mode electromagnetic waves. Because TE-mode scattering can be reduced to the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation, solvers based on the hierarchically semiseparable (HSS) representation are highly attractive due to their high parallel efficiency. However, as the HSS representation applies low-rank approximations to all off-diagonal blocks, it exhibits poor compatibility with high-order discretization methods. We developed a fast direct solver with [MATH] convergence for Helmholtz transmission problems, whereas conventional HSS solvers typically yield only [MATH] convergence (where [MATH] represents intervals between the quadrature nodes). It is based on the weakly singular Burton-Miller boundary integral equation and the Nystr\"om method with a one-point correction. Furthermore, recognizing that matrix component calculation, rather than matrix factorization, dominates the total computational time of HSS-type boundary integral solvers, we introduced a load-balancing method to maximize parallel efficiency. Numerical results demonstrate that the direct solver achieves high-accuracy convergence and nearly ideal strong and weak scalabilities.
tldr: This paper presents a fast direct solver for TE-mode electromagnetic scattering using HSS representations and parallel computing.
motivation: Efficient and accurate solvers for electromagnetic scattering problems are needed for engineering applications.
method: The solver uses a hierarchically semiseparable (HSS) representation with a weakly singular Burton-Miller boundary integral equation and Nyström method, parallelized with MPI/OpenMP.
result: The solver achieves high-accuracy convergence and nearly ideal strong and weak scalabilities on distributed memory systems.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective for TE-mode scattering problems and demonstrates good parallel performance.

title: Geometric Reduced-Attitude Tracking Under A Time-Varying Conic Constraint Via Smooth Reference-Shaping
authors: Pedro Santos, Joel Reis, Paulo Oliveira, Carlos Silvestre
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter studies reduced-attitude tracking for a rigid body on the 2-sphere S2 under a time-varying conic constraint. Using a kinematic model on S2, we first propose a geometric tracking law that guarantees almostglobal asymptotic and regionally exponential convergence in the unconstrained case, where the angular velocity serves as the control input. We then introduce a smooth reference-shaping mechanism that adjusts the desired direction so that the reference provided to the controller satisfies the time-varying conic constraint while preserving the smoothness required by the tracking law. The resulting approach yields smooth continuous feedback and retains the stability guarantees of the unconstrained controller, albeit at the expense of enforcing a soft version of the original constraint. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the method and highlight its suitability for applications where deterministic behavior, smooth control action, and strong stability guarantees are preferred over hard constraint satisfaction.
tldr: This paper presents a geometric tracking law for reduced-attitude control on S2 with a time-varying conic constraint, using smooth reference-shaping to ensure constraint satisfaction.
motivation: Reduced-attitude tracking under conic constraints is important for applications like UAVs and spacecraft, but existing methods often lack smoothness or strong stability guarantees.
method: A geometric tracking law on S2 is designed for unconstrained case, then a smooth reference-shaping mechanism adjusts the desired direction to satisfy the time-varying conic constraint while preserving smoothness.
result: The approach achieves almost-global asymptotic and regional exponential stability in the unconstrained case, and enforces a soft version of the constraint with retained stability guarantees.
conclusion: The method is suitable for applications requiring deterministic behavior, smooth control, and strong stability, though it only enforces a soft constraint.

title: Optimal Control Problem For Reflected McKean--Vlasov Stochastic Differential Equations With Poisson Jumps
authors: Kai Wang Wenrui Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the optimal relaxed control problem for a class of one-dimensional reflected McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations with Poisson jumps. Due to the presence of the jump term, the state process generally belongs to the Skorokhod space [MATH], which makes the proof of tightness and the passage to the limit more complicated. Under Lipschitz conditions and suitable growth conditions, we establish uniform moment estimates for the state process and the reflecting process. Then, by using Aldous' tightness criterion, the continuity of the Skorokhod map, and the stability results for stochastic integrals, we prove the existence of an optimal relaxed control. Furthermore, under the Roxin convexity condition, we prove the existence of a strict optimal control. In the general case, we show that relaxed controls can be approximated by a sequence of strict controls.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control for reflected McKean-Vlasov stochastic differential equations with Poisson jumps, a topic in stochastic control theory.
motivation: To establish existence of optimal relaxed and strict controls for a class of reflected McKean-Vlasov SDEs with jumps, which are important in finance and engineering.
method: Uses Aldous' tightness criterion, continuity of the Skorokhod map, and stability results for stochastic integrals under Lipschitz and growth conditions.
result: Proves existence of an optimal relaxed control, and under Roxin convexity condition, existence of a strict optimal control; also shows relaxed controls can be approximated by strict controls.
conclusion: The paper extends optimal control theory to reflected McKean-Vlasov SDEs with Poisson jumps, providing theoretical foundations for applications.

title: From Welfare To Utility: Generalized Objectives In Budget-Feasible Procurement
authors: Alon Eden, Eldar Kerner, Kira Goldner, Thodoris Tsilivis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study mechanism design for the budget-feasible procurement problem, a natural problem that arises when a buyer wants to procure goods or services from multiple strategic sellers who each have a cost to provide that service, the buyer has a value for each service procured, but is constrained by a budget. In contrast to prior work, which has focused on buyer value maximization for this problem, we solve for optimal and approximately-optimal mechanisms for the objectives of buyer utility (value of procured services minus payments), welfare (value minus production costs), and generalizations of the two. For welfare, we design a simple mechanism that obtains a constant-factor approximation for the prior-free (worst-case) setting. As prior-free mechanisms fail to provide any guarantee for utility, even for a single seller, we consider Bayesian settings, where the buyer has distributional knowledge over sellers' costs. We first provide a utility-optimal mechanism that satisfies the buyer's budget constraint in expectation, then we show how to modify the mechanism to satisfy the budget constraint ex-post, for every realization of seller costs, while still obtaining near-optimal utility guarantees. Finally, we generalize our mechanisms to other objectives.
tldr: This paper studies mechanism design for budget-feasible procurement, focusing on objectives beyond value maximization such as buyer utility and welfare.
motivation: Prior work on budget-feasible procurement only considered buyer value maximization, but in practice buyers may care about utility or welfare.
method: The authors design mechanisms for welfare in a prior-free setting and for utility in Bayesian settings, with both ex-ante and ex-post budget constraints.
result: They achieve constant-factor approximations for welfare and near-optimal utility guarantees, and generalize to other objectives.
conclusion: The paper extends the theory of budget-feasible procurement to more realistic objectives, providing simple and effective mechanisms.

title: Data Sharing And Competition In Learning-by-Deploying Industries: Insights From Robotics And Beyond
authors: Luca-Andrei Manea Yunjin Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many modern technologies improve through use. Each unit deployed generates data that trains the next generation, so deployment is both production and an investment in a shared learning stock. We study how the architecture of this learning, whether pooled across firms or fragmented within them, interacts with firms' deployment decisions and with product-market competition. In a two-period model, symmetric firms make irreversible capacity choices, and capacity in use feeds a learning curve that raises future productivity. We call this learning-by-deploying, replacing the production experience of the classic learning-by-doing tradition with deployment-generated data. With exogenous prices, pooling raises welfare but firms underinvest in early deployment. Downstream Cournot competition overturns this: pooling depresses the price, so the private value of sharing falls with competition and can turn negative. We characterize a sustainability threshold governed, under general demand, by the elasticity of industry demand over the output range pooling induces, and confirm the patterns numerically.
tldr: This paper studies how data sharing and competition interact in industries where products improve through deployment-generated data, using a two-period model with learning-by-deploying.
motivation: Many modern technologies improve through use, generating data that trains future generations. The paper aims to understand how the architecture of learning (pooled vs. fragmented) affects firms' deployment decisions and product-market competition.
method: The authors develop a two-period model with symmetric firms making irreversible capacity choices, where capacity in use feeds a learning curve that raises future productivity. They analyze the effects of data pooling under exogenous prices and downstream Cournot competition.
result: With exogenous prices, pooling raises welfare but firms underinvest in early deployment. Under Cournot competition, pooling depresses prices, reducing the private value of sharing, which can become negative. A sustainability threshold is characterized based on the elasticity of industry demand.
conclusion: The architecture of learning-by-deploying significantly impacts welfare and firm incentives, with competition potentially undermining the benefits of data sharing.

title: Knowing Who, Not How Much: Learning-Augmented Mechanisms For Consumer Utility Maximization
authors: Kira Goldner, Divyarthi Mohan, Thodoris Tsilivis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study consumer utility maximization in an online random-order model where strategic agents arrive sequentially. To circumvent strong impossibility results for utility maximization, we turn to the framework of learning-augmented mechanism design. Crucially, we show that the types of predictions commonly used in learning-augmented mechanism design (such as predictions of agent values or the optimal value) are not useful for utility maximization, where payments are directly at odds with the objective. Instead, we identify that a qualitatively different kind of prediction suffices: the identity of the highest-valued agent. First, we provide a deterministic truthful mechanism for our online setting by adapting offline randomized techniques. Then, we augment our mechanism with predictions. When the predictions are correct, we achieve a constant approximation to the optimal solution under full information (consistency), and even when predictions are arbitrarily bad, we guarantee a constant approximation to the best implementable solution (robustness).
tldr: This paper studies online consumer utility maximization using learning-augmented mechanism design, with predictions of the highest-valued agent's identity.
motivation: Strong impossibility results exist for utility maximization in online settings, so the authors seek to leverage predictions to circumvent them.
method: They adapt offline randomized techniques to design a deterministic truthful mechanism, then augment it with a prediction of the highest-valued agent's identity.
result: When predictions are correct, the mechanism achieves constant approximation to the optimal full-information solution; even with arbitrary errors, it guarantees constant approximation to the best implementable solution.
conclusion: Predicting the identity of the highest-valued agent, rather than values, is effective for utility maximization in online mechanism design.

title: A Non-Line-of-Sight, Multi-Modality-based Side-Channel Ip Theft Attack On Additive Manufacturing Using Dual Smartphones
authors: Amirhossein Jamarani, Diba Afroze, Yazhou Tu, Mark Yampolskiy, Xiali Hei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.00186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) has revolutionized major sectors, including aerospace, automotive, and healthcare, by enabling adjustable production. As the usage of AM increases, so does the risk of Intellectual Property (IP) leakage during the printing process due to unintended side-channel emissions.
